title: KT Signal Connector API v1 host frame

proxyGroupId.description: Proxy group identifier (ADR 0001, Phase 4). 'default' is the reserved, always-present group; additional groups are defined by the trusted launcher at connector spawn and are never created over IPC. An omitted proxyGroup means 'default'.

params.description: No parameters (contract revision 1.117, §4.98, capability group-invite-links): the 16-byte CSPRNG link password is account-less material (the official generateGroupInviteLinkPassword). Read lane; the bytes are single-pass material — they ride the answer and are never logged or persisted. The result is {password} — standard base64 of exactly 16 bytes (24 chars).

proxyGroup.description: Optional target proxy group for the account being linked; fixed for the life of the link once link.finish succeeds. An unknown group fails with PROXY_GROUP_NOT_FOUND. A pre-Phase-4 connector rejects this field with INVALID_REQUEST (deny_unknown_fields), so hosts must feature-detect via runtime.status first.

accountsUpdateConfigurationParams.description: Update the account's official settings (contract revision 1.46, §4.45; linkPreviews since 1.120 §4.101, capability account-settings): at least one of readReceipts / typingIndicators / phoneNumberSharingMode / unlistedPhoneNumber / linkPreviews must be present; only the provided keys are forwarded upstream and written (official updateConfiguration partial-write semantics — the upstream writes exactly the provided fields, reads the rest back untouched), and an all-fields-satisfied call is an idempotent no-write success. A call with no writable key answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. phoneNumberSharingMode takes "everybody" | "nobody" (the official AccountRecord PhoneNumberSharingMode values; the old CONTACTS_ONLY has been removed from the official proto and is not accepted). linkPreviews is the account-level link-preview auto-generation bit (the official AccountRecord field 11; a change made by another linked device arrives through the settings.configurationSync event). The result is {status: 'saved'} on a definite success. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable).

readReceipts.description: Whether the account sends read receipts. Optional; omitted means no change upstream.

typingIndicators.description: Whether the account sends typing indicators. Optional; omitted means no change upstream.

phoneNumberSharingMode.description: Who may discover the account by phone number: "everybody" or "nobody" (official AccountRecord values; CONTACTS_ONLY is gone from the official proto). Optional; omitted means no change upstream.

unlistedPhoneNumber.description: Whether the phone number is unlisted from discovery. Optional; omitted means no change upstream.

linkPreviews.description: Whether the account auto-generates link previews (official AccountRecord field 11; contract 1.120, §4.101). Optional; omitted means no change upstream. The §4.87 settings.configurationSync event carries the same key when another linked device changes it.

accountsSetProfileParams.description: Write the account's profile (contract revision 1.46, §4.45, capability account-settings): the text face is a full write exactly like the official updateProfile — every upstream write carries the complete profile, so a text key the caller omits is cleared upstream (the desktop always sends the full text face it wants). givenName is required, 1..128 bytes (the official desktop ProfileEditor maxBytes for both name components); familyName ≤ 128 bytes; about ≤ 512 bytes (the official bio byte budget); emoji ≤ 32 bytes, one emoji. avatar has three states: absent = keep the current avatar, a data:image/*;base64, URI with ≤ 10 MiB decoded = replace, explicit null = remove. The result is {status: 'saved'} on a definite success. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: avatar upload failures fold into STORAGE_WRITE_FAILED and the STORAGE_* family passes through verbatim (retryable).

givenName.description: Required profile first name; the full-write anchor (an empty string is INVALID_REQUEST).

familyName.description: Optional profile last name; omitted (or null) clears it upstream — official full-write semantics.

about.description: Optional profile bio; omitted (or null) clears it upstream — official full-write semantics.

emoji.description: Optional single bio emoji; omitted (or null) clears it upstream — official full-write semantics.

avatar.description: Three states: absent = keep the current avatar; a data:image/*;base64, data URI whose decoded size is 1..10485760 bytes (10 MiB, the engine's stated avatar budget, AvatarHelper-scale) = replace; explicit null = remove (reachable since contract 1.90 — the 1.46 Option<Value> shape folded JSON null into absence, and the schema widened to null the same revision). The maxLength is the padded-base64 encoding of the ceiling plus a fixed prefix margin — the connector enforces the decoded budget itself and answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call.

accountsSetExpireTimerParams.description: Set or clear the account's disappearing-message default timer (contract revision 1.46, §4.45, capability account-settings) — the official universal timer (AccountRecord.universalExpireTimer). 0 turns it off; a same-value set is an idempotent no-write upstream. Unlike conversations.setExpireTimer this is the account-level default: new conversations inherit it, per-conversation timers stay on conversations.setExpireTimer, and the universal timer carries no expiration-update broadcast (other devices converge through storage sync). expireSeconds is 0..4294967295 (the engine face validates within u32 and the official field is uint32; unlike the per-conversation face there is no signal-cli int counterpart to share a smaller denominator with). The result is {status: 'saved'} on a definite success. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable).

expireSeconds.description: The account-wide default timer in seconds; 0 turns it off.

accountsSetUsernameParams.description: Set or delete the account's Signal username (contract revision 1.59, §4.55, capability username) — the pinned signal-cli updateAccount mutually exclusive group (username XOR deleteUsername; the schema cannot express XOR so both stay optional and the service ladder enforces exactly-one, answering INVALID_REQUEST when both are present or both absent). username grammar is the official desktop shape mirrored fail-closed: nickname [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*, optional discriminator .N all-digits 0-65535 with no 00-leading and a 0-leading form only as exactly two digits, 3..32 characters total (the pinned libsignal bounds, AccountHelper.java:363-364); a bare nickname (no dot) is allowed and lets the server pick the discriminator. The server reserve/confirm remains the authority. The face (contract 1.75, §4.66) orchestrates the engine's two-hop usernameReserve→usernameConfirm under the same mutating discipline (each hop is a separate mutating call: an indeterminate hop answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and nothing retries; the adopted candidate wins — a bare nickname's discriminator is the server's pick). Structured server codes (contract 1.75): USERNAME_TAKEN (reserve 409 / confirm 410) and USERNAME_RESERVATION_GONE (confirm 409 — the reservation expired or lost its race; reserve again) answer retryable=false; USERNAME_RATE_LIMITED (413/429) and USERNAME_SERVER_FAILED (anything else) answer retryable=true; the honest partial-success face — the server confirmed but the engine's storage write failed — rides the STORAGE_* family (the username is live server-side; getUsername / storage sync converge). No case-change shortcut: every set rides the full two-hop. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: the result projects the upstream write-back {username, usernameLink?} on the set path (the connector's only username read face — there is no local-account username getter in the pinned signal-cli) and {} on the delete path; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Nothing is persisted connector-side; the desktop mirrors from the write-back.

username.description: The full username (nickname plus optional .discriminator) or a bare nickname. The whole-string wire bound is 38 (the 3..32 nickname window plus the separator and the widest discriminator digit run); the grammar below the wire bound — nickname charset, discriminator forms — is enforced connector-side and answers INVALID_REQUEST.

deleteUsername.description: Delete the account's username; mutually exclusive with username.

accountsGetUsernameParams.description: Read the account's own username (contract revision 1.59, §4.55; the face opened with contract 1.74, §4.65; capability username). The face routes the engine's getUsername reader (the AccountRecord username(33)/usernameLink(35) storage truth, engine compat §3) and answers {username, usernameLink} with both fields null when the account never set one — the unset state is the answer, not an error. Read lane.

accountsDeviceCapabilitiesParams.description: Register and read back the account's device-face capabilities (contract revision 1.100, §4.81). The face dispatches the engine's idempotent deviceCapabilities registration (the official registerCapabilities endpoint, PUT — repeating the call repeats the same server-side declaration, the official every-start semantics) and answers {registered, capabilities}: the engine's bare account identity never crosses the connector (the answer strips the account key), and the capability bits ride verbatim — the connector invents no keys and strips none (the official CapabilitiesUploadType key set, additive). Every engine failure folds to UPSTREAM_ERROR (unknown/unregistered account, 401 unlink, server failure all collapse engine-side); this face extends no matcher of its own — the §4.17 unlink chain stays the engine-event worker's job. Read lane, account-scoped mutating serialization (the contacts.sync precedent: the upstream face is a PUT). No local persistence.

accountsGetDevicesParams.description: List the account's linked devices (contract revision 1.122, §4.103, capability device-management): the engine GET v1/devices projection — the server list in server order, including the account's own primary device — with the engine-side device-name decryption (the official encryptDeviceName pair, decrypted with the account's own ACI identity key; an encrypted name that is absent or undecryptable answers no `name` key — the honest no-name face, the official decrypt-failure domain). The result is {devices: [{deviceId, name?, registrationId?, lastSeenMs?, createdAtCiphertext?}]}: deviceId is the positive server id (1..4294967295), lastSeenMs is the epoch-ms server stamp, createdAtCiphertext is the server's opaque base64 flag material riding verbatim. Bounded projection: at most 32 entries (entries beyond truncate); an entry whose deviceId is non-numeric drops; a projected deviceId of 0 fails the whole face INVALID_REQUEST — 0 is the libsignal no-device hole, never a real server device, and a list claiming it must not cross the connector. Unknown account answers ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. Structured engine errors: DEVICES_FAILED (server refusal, retryable=false; error.data.status carries the server HTTP status verbatim when the server gave one), DEVICES_UNAVAILABLE (network/transport, retryable=true). Read lane, non-mutating; no local persistence, no logging.

accountsUnlinkDeviceParams.description: Unlink one linked device server-side (contract revision 1.122, §4.103, capability device-management): the engine DELETE v1/devices/{id} — the official unlink endpoint — with the server owning the authorization (a primary unlinks any linked device, a linked device unlinks only itself; the over-reach and primary-delete refusals surface as DEVICES_FAILED with error.data.status carrying the server HTTP status). deviceId is the positive server device id as accounts.getDevices projected it (1..4294967295); 0 is refused INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call (the libsignal no-device hole, never a real device). The result is {status: 'unlinked'} on the definite success. The unlink converges to the account's other devices through the official device-link sync — the connector adds no local unlink mirror and answers no local device list beyond accounts.getDevices; the §4.17 unlink chain (the account's own device being unlinked remotely) stays the engine-event worker's job. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried (an unlink whose delivery is unknown may already have happened server-side). Structured engine errors: DEVICES_FAILED (server refusal, retryable=false, data.status? verbatim), DEVICES_UNAVAILABLE (network/transport, retryable=true).

deviceId.description: The positive server device id to unlink, as accounts.getDevices projected it.

usernameLookupParams.description: Resolve usernames or username-link URLs against the account's own engine session (contract revision 1.59, §4.55; the kt-engine face opened with contract 1.74, §4.65; capability username). Entries are full usernames or username-link URLs, not bare nicknames. usernames carries 1..20 entries (KT bound for one host frame; the upstream takes an open array), each 1..64 characters, forwarded verbatim. The result projects the upstream array entry-for-entry: {results: [{recipient, number?, username?, uuid?, isRegistered}]} — uuid != null means the entry resolved to a registered account (uuid == null with isRegistered=false is the unregistered face). The upstream CDSI face can rate-limit (RateLimitException) which surfaces as UPSTREAM_ERROR. Read lane. The face dispatches the engine's usernameLookup reader — the same frame, the same anonymous server lookups (hash/link resolution), per-entry failures arrive pre-degraded (isRegistered=false). The desktop has no lookup UI in this batch: the face is wire-complete for a later batch.

usernames.description: Usernames or username-link URLs to resolve, 1..20 entries.

phoneLookupParams.description: Resolve full E.164 phone numbers against the account's own engine session — its CDSI (Contact Discovery Service) face (contract revision 1.164, §4.162; the kt-engine face is the phoneLookup reader, engine d088a59; capability phone-lookup). The account key is `account` on this face (the D-batch desktop wire lock, desktop commit 64584c27 — username.lookup carries the same opaque id under `accountId`). numbers carries 1..20 entries (the engine's own frame bound mirrored; a small batch is rate-limit politeness — the CDSI threshold is unpublished), each a complete E.164 number ^\+\d{7,15}$ (a leading + and 7..15 ASCII digits): the connector mirrors the grammar fail-closed before any engine traffic and the engine's PHONE_INVALID face stays the authority. The result projects the upstream array entry-for-entry: {entries: [{number, aci?, pni?, isRegistered}]} — number is the entry echoed verbatim, aci/pni are the engine's single-hit service-id projections (the official directory.rs double-hit takes the ACI), absent means no hit on that id, and a miss/unregistered entry arrives pre-degraded ({number, isRegistered: false}, the usernameLookup discipline) — no entry is ever dropped. Read lane; zero local persistence — the projection answers from the engine's memory face alone, nothing lands in the connector store, and the number→account local mapping stays the contacts sync chain's. Error faces (engine d088a59): PHONE_INVALID (deterministic E.164 refusal, retryable=false), PHONE_RATE_LIMITED (CDSI 429-family, carries data.retryAfterSeconds — the server's retry-after seconds verbatim, the wait decision is the caller's, nothing retries automatically), PHONE_SERVER_FAILED (the remaining server/connection family, details withheld, retryable=true); the unknown-account face stays the plain -32603 → UPSTREAM_ERROR ladder. The desktop D-batch (64584c27) consumes the face behind the phone-lookup tag — find-by-phone-number in the new-chat compose flow.

items.description: One complete E.164 phone number (+ and 7..15 ASCII digits), forwarded verbatim.

numbers.description: Full E.164 numbers to resolve, 1..20 entries (the engine's own frame bound mirrored).

phoneLookupResult.description: The phone.lookup answer (contract revision 1.164, §4.162): the engine's CDSI projection entry-for-entry in input order, keys riding the engine's names verbatim — the connector re-keys nothing (null folds to absence, the repo no-null discipline). Zero local persistence: the answer is a memory projection only.

aci.description: The ACI service-id UUID when the CDSI hit resolved an ACI; absent (never null) when not.

pni.description: The PNI service-id UUID when the CDSI hit resolved a PNI; absent (never null) when not. Single-hit semantics: the official double-hit face takes the ACI.

isRegistered.description: Whether the entry resolved to a registered account; a miss/unregistered entry arrives pre-degraded {number, isRegistered: false}.

entries.description: One entry per input number, input order, capped at 20 by the params gate; no entry is ever dropped.

conversationsListParams.description: Read lane over the local conversation cache; ordered by newest message, page-bounded, cursor-resumable. Contract 1.43 (§4.42): the result includes the linked account's own Note to Self direct conversation — the contacts sync no longer drops the self entry, so its skeleton materializes like any contact's — and every summary row carries isSelf (always-serialized boolean): true exactly for the direct conversation whose peerKey equals the account's own number (number-based, the §4.24 boundary: the own ACI is not queryable upstream, so a UUID-keyed row cannot be marked), false on every other row including groups. The self row's title is raw contact material (the account's own profile name); the desktop localizes the Note to Self title and avatar from isSelf — the connector ships no copy. Contract 1.60 (§4.52): every summary row carries isTerminated (plain bool, present only when true — absent on false, pre-1.60 hosts read byte-identical rows): the group termination flag the 1.53 §4.50 appendix sync capture stores in the kind='group' contacts row, stamped at read time (a group and its contacts row share the stable id; a group with no cache row yet, every direct row, and every pre-1.53 sync row answer absent/false). The desktop forward-target filter consumes it (the official selectors/composable face excludes terminated groups); the receive chain cannot refresh the flag, only the next contacts.sync can, and syncedAt remains the staleness signal. Contract 1.65 (§4.58): every summary row carries messageRequestAccepted (bare always-serialized boolean, the muted/pinned/isSelf discipline — both values are meaningful): the official isConversationAccepted multi-factor derived at read time over the row's stored engine factor stamp (mrr_factors_json — {hidden, profileSharing, blocked} the throttled listContacts enrich stamps on its existing round trip, schema version 20; an engine without the flags stamps the probed-absent {}), the message window, and isSelf. Contract 1.70 (§4.58 consume batch): the stamp also carries the authoritative acceptResponseType face (the official factor's first weight) that a linked device's syncMessage.messageRequestResponse mirror writes on ingest — a well-formed mirror (known non-UNKNOWN enum member, exactly one thread leg, the ServiceId UUID / 32-byte base64 shapes) stamps it, everything else fails closed into the plain skip; a stamped ACCEPT accepts ahead of every window weight, any other member keeps the window answer, and a row without the stamp keeps the 1.65 local fallback verbatim. Honest per-factor holes never invented (each collapses to inactive, the official default posture): messageCountBeforeMessageRequests (official-desktop migration state), and the group factors addedBy/pendingAdminApprovalV2/group profileSharing (no engine read face) — a group row derives accepted from its own outgoing window alone. A desktop consumes the key as authoritative when present and keeps its local window derivation only for pre-1.65 connectors where the key is absent. Contract 1.71 (2026-10-07, dated note — the desktop evidence-gate data-plane gap, desktop matrix §18.4 2026-10-06 record): every summary row also carries hasUserInitiatedOutbound (bare always-serialized boolean, the muted/pinned/isSelf discipline — both values are meaningful): true exactly when the conversation's whole history contains at least one outgoing data row — the official sentMessageCount > 0 factor (ts/util/isConversationAccepted.preload.ts:58,75, the same factor weight the §4.58 derivation reads) surfaced as a standalone bit, aligned with the official hasUserInitiatedMessages whole-history EXISTS semantics (Server.node.ts:2389-2410, Interface.std.ts:486, conversations.preload.ts:4621/:3752-3755, maybeForwardMessages.preload.ts:192-201), independent of any message window or the newest row. Derived at read time (the same read-time family as messageRequestAccepted, list page and single-row conversation.changed summary share one helper); pure wire addition — pre-1.71 hosts read byte-identical rows without it. Absent store evidence (a fresh row, or any history the connector does not hold) projects false — honest absence, never invented. Contract 1.138 (§4.129): every summary row additively carries its protocol identifiers, derived at read time from the peer key's shape so the desktop's `!` selector faces match without a second lookup — groupId (a group row, the raw group master key, the §4.44/§4.50 addressing form), e164 (a direct row keyed on a +prefixed phone number), serviceId (a direct row keyed on a ServiceId UUID, or keyed on a number-shaped key mapped through the most recent ingest-written peer_identities row); a key nothing resolves leaves all three absent (the row stays addressable by id, no identifier invented) and pni is reserved-never-present (the connector has no PNI source — the honest hole §4.129 documents). Contract 1.138 (§4.131): every summary row also carries blocked (bare always-serialized boolean, the muted/pinned/isSelf discipline): the direct row's stored blocked stamp — written by the §4.47 setBlocked write-back, the §4.58 BLOCK-family request-response verbs (BLOCK=3/BLOCK_AND_DELETE=4/BLOCK_AND_SPAM=6), and the contacts enrich's own isBlocked — so the desktop renders the mask state from the list/event stream instead of a pull; group rows stay false (§4.45 pull remains the group authority, the honest hole). Contract 1.138 (§4.130): every summary row also carries draftTimestamp (epoch ms, absent when nothing is drafted or after conversations.clearDraft) — the official DraftRepository record's clock, the only draft material the connector holds (draft text stays desktop-side safeStorage); written by the new local conversations.saveDraft/conversations.clearDraft faces, and the refreshed summary rides conversation.changed on every write. Contract 1.146 (§4.144): the serviceId derivation widens — a direct row keyed on a +prefixed number now also maps through the most recent ingest-written peer_identities row (either spelling, the dual-form number normalization: the exact form probes first, the alternate only on a miss), so such a row answers e164 and serviceId together; a key nothing resolves keeps the pre-1.146 answer verbatim and pni stays reserved-never-present. The sync-contacts ingest (§4.122, same revision) lands a numbered record's ACI into that table through the §4.37 receive-chain write, so a contact that never showed up on a live envelope resolves too; wire additive, pre-1.146 hosts read byte-identical rows.

messagesListParams.description: Contract 1.72 (2026-10-07, the §4.64 bodyRanges pass-through; the receive half of §4.62): every projected message row carries the peer's text-formatting ranges as an optional `textStyles: [{style, start, length}]` array on the flattened MessageRecord — the §4.20 vocabulary (BOLD / ITALIC / STRIKETHROUGH / MONOSPACE / SPOILER) over UTF-16 code-unit offsets, persisted in the row's rich payload since 1.25 and now a guaranteed contract face on every read shape (`message.upserted` and `messages.search` share it). The same per-entry gate the §4.20 receive face has practiced holds end to end: only the five renderable styles pass, NONE and unknown values drop individually (a hostile payload can never fail the message), start/length are u32-bounded, the list caps at 64 entries, and an all-invalid list collapses to the key-absent plain row — absence means unstyled; rows without styles (and every pre-1.25 row) read byte-identical without the key. No body-bounds gate runs on either face (the official parseTextStyles posture). Contract 1.107 (2026-10-11, the §4.88 ingest key-list completion; the receive half of the engine's P14 live-projection batch): the attachment descriptor gains the engine's P14 metadata keys verbatim — the render `caption`, the blur preview `blurHash` (non-empty only), the streaming-integrity pair `incrementalMac` + `chunkSize` (both or neither, the official filePointers.preload.ts:84-87 discipline) and the always-boolean `isBorderless` / `isGif` projections beside `isVoiceNote` (no flag bit = false; the media-type judgement stays the desktop's) — the link-preview card gains its `date` publish stamp (positive only, the official falsy posture), the rich payload gains `dataMessage.expireTimerVersion` (positive, u32-bounded; the timer value itself stays the row's `expireSeconds` face) and the sent mirror's three transcript faces (`isRecipientUpdate`, `unidentifiedStatus[]`, `storyMessageRecipients[]` — verbatim, receive dataMessages never carry them). All keys are per-key fail-closed at the engine's own projection shapes: a hostile or zero-information key answers absent (or false, for the boolean trio), an over-bound identity or key material drops per-key, the outer lists take the sync receive family's 256-entry cap, and every pre-1.107 row reads byte-identical (the new descriptor keys stay absent; the boolean trio serializes explicit false, the isVoiceNote shape). The archive import face parses the same-named keys and flag bits, so imported and live descriptors share one wire form. Contract 1.139 (§4.132): the row's optional `contact` card face — the §4.38 bounded card the archive import rows have carried since 1.78 — now also rides live receive and sent-mirror rows: the engine's `dataMessage.contact` / `syncMessage.sentMessage.contact` faces parse through the same import authority (the MAX_CONTACT_* bounds, the HOME/MOBILE/WORK/CUSTOM type vocabulary, the whole-card discipline — no usable content, no face), the live-wrapped avatar pointer `{avatar, isProfile}` unwrapping onto the descriptor list (byte fetches stay on the existing media channel; `isProfile` — the engine's address-book fact — never rides the row), and a bodyless card lands as a real incoming/outgoing message row (a card beside a control echo keeps its control routing). Wire additive-only: live rows begin carrying the `contact` key the import rows already carried; pre-1.139 hosts read pre-1.139 rows byte-identically and simply never saw live cards. Contract 1.150 (2026-10-14, §4.149; the receive half of the engine's voice-waveform batch b656714): the attachment descriptor gains the engine's voice-waveform pair verbatim — `waveform`, the outbound voice note's render buckets as standard base64 (the engine generates a fixed 100-byte 0..255 dB vector on every `;voice=true` send, non-empty only) and `duration`, the float seconds. Engine-generated, never interpreted connector-side: no base64 validation, no re-encoding, and no pair gate — the pairing (both keys or neither, a failed generation ships neither and the send still goes) is the engine's generation invariant the connector deliberately does not enforce, it forwards whatever is stated per key. The ingest shape gates stay the §4.88 posture: an empty or over-bound (512-char, the locator base64 family) waveform drops whole (never truncated into unusable render material), a non-number or non-positive duration answers absent. The archive import face structurally never carries the pair (the backup FilePointer proto has no such members), so import rows keep their pre-1.150 descriptors byte-identical and every pre-1.150 live row reads byte-identical too (the keys stay absent). Contract 1.160 (2026-10-15, §4.158; the receive half of the own-story sync transcript): the row gains the optional event-only story face — `isStory` (bare always-serialized boolean, present only when true) and `storyMessage` (the engine's `sentMessage.storyMessage` projection verbatim, the same bounded face the story.received event forwards — textAttachment (with optional text/textStyle/preview/mentions/textStyles/color faces) or fileAttachment with the locator full-face, plus allowsReplies and the optional profileKey/group context), the pair riding together exactly when the account's own multi-device transcript lands. The face is event-payload-only: stories stay rowless in the store (the §4.67 posture), so no stored row and no read-lane row ever carries either key — only the one `message.upserted` emission the desktop's story intercept consumes (the outgoing direction lands the row under the self sender key). The connector never parses the story body; a group face rides verbatim and stays the desktop shape-gate's call (the v1 group-story non-consumption is the desktop's recorded boundary). Every pre-1.160 row and every stored row reads byte-identically (both keys stay absent). Contract 1.178 (§4.178, the inbound quote deep link): a row's stored `quote_snapshot` resolves to the local row it names on every read face and on the live `message.upserted` event — same `sent_at` as the snapshot's upstream id, author checked through the store's own identity derivations — surfacing the target's row id through the read-time `quoteMessageId` (never stored; the stored column keeps its send-face-only meaning, §4.171 discipline). An unresolved snapshot stays honestly absent: the official `referencedMessageNotFound` face (no network backfill — the official client re-runs the same local by-sentAt lookup at render time), which the desktop renders as the quote warning strip. A retracted target still resolves (jump to the tombstone); an out-of-order target self-heals on the next read.

messagesAdjacentMediaParams.description: Contract 1.93 (§4.76): the adjacent visual-media probe behind the desktop lightbox's cross-message navigation — the official getOlder/NewerMessagesByConversation probe with requireVisualMediaAttachments (Signal-Desktop ts/state/ducks/lightbox.preload.ts showLightboxForAdjacentMessage, Server.node.ts getAdjacentMessagesByConversation) projected onto the connector's store. The anchor is a message id the caller already holds (the current lightbox item's message); it resolves to its stored sent_at or the call answers INVALID_REQUEST retryable=false — a vanished anchor is never silently re-anchored. direction 'older' walks toward the conversation's past, 'newer' toward its present; the anchor row itself is never returned (the official requireDifferentMessage posture). The result is {items: MessageRecord[]} ordered adjacency-first (the row closest to the anchor first), each row carrying at least one attachment with an image/* or video/* content type — the desktop lightbox strip's own predicate — with view-once rows always excluded (the §4.37 boundary: tap-to-view media never joins a navigation strip); story rows need no predicate because a story never lands in the messages table at all (§4.67). Rows come in the messages.list stored shape (reactions and edits attached the same way), read in bounded keyset chunks until limit matches accumulate or the range exhausts — an empty items array is the honest 'no more media in this direction' answer. Store-only read: no upstream traffic, and deliberately no unread-clearing side effect (probing the lightbox's neighbors is not viewing the thread). Advertised through the message-adjacent-media capability tag.

messagesSearchParams.description: Contract 1.30: account-wide substring search over stored message bodies. Empty or whitespace-only queries answer an empty page; queries over 128 characters are rejected (INVALID_REQUEST). Contract 1.72 (§4.64): hit rows carry the same optional `textStyles` ranges as messages.list — one stored shape, every read face agrees. Contract 1.162 (§4.160): the optional `conversationId` scopes the same read to one conversation — the official search-in-conversation posture (the header search action carries `conversation.id`) — as a pure filter over the same newest-first ordering and the same account-bound cursor format; an unknown conversation answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND (the messages.list ladder) ahead of the query normalization, and the key absent keeps the account-wide search byte-identically. The hit rows already carry the deep-link identity face the official result row consumes (id + conversationId + sentAt, showConversation({conversationId, messageId: id})) — no result-face key was added or needed.

conversationId.description: Contract 1.162 (§4.160): optional conversation scope — present scopes the search to that conversation (unknown answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND), absent keeps the account-wide search byte-identically.

messagesSendTextParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). mentions (contract revision 1.34) is the optional outbound @mention list: at most 64 entries (extras are dropped, the §4.20 receive cap mirrored); number resolves contacts-first with ACI/UUID passthrough — an entry whose number resolves to nothing local is dropped (the official behavior for unresolvable mention addresses), and an empty number fails closed INVALID_REQUEST; start/length are UTF-16 code-unit offsets the caller indexes against its own body (the official BodyRange semantics). textStyle (contract revision 1.69) is the optional text-formatting range list over the same body — it fails closed (unknown style / over 64 entries INVALID_REQUEST) and a retry rebuilds the send without it. storyReplyAuthor/storyReplyTimestamp (contract revision 1.156, §4.154) are the optional story-reply send context (the engine send frame's storyContext, the official DataMessage.StoryContext alignment): the connector forwards each key verbatim only when the caller sent it, and the pair discipline (both-present or both-absent; a single-sided presence refused) plus the whole value domain (empty author, zero/negative/fractional/non-integer timestamp, an unresolvable author) are the engine's fail-closed parse answering plain -32603 → UPSTREAM_ERROR (retryable) — never a connector gate. The context is transit-only: it rides the engine frame, never the pending row, so a messages.retryText rebuild resends without it. Contract revision 1.173 (§4.173): a group-addressed send's answer row carries sendOutcomes {succeeded, failed} — the engine reply's per-recipient `results` array counted into entry totals (direct sends and shapeless replies keep the key absent, pre-1.173 wire parity). A group send where every results entry failed delivers nothing: the row settles definitively failed (no automatic retry schedule; the manual Retry Send face stays) and the call answers GROUP_SEND_FAILED (retryable=true). A mixed send keeps the sent row and the counts — the desktop derives the official partial-sent arm from them.

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

text.description: Non-empty text; the service authoritatively enforces at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

number.description: The mentioned address: a phone number (resolved against the local contacts cache, digit-suffix rule) or a UUID-shaped ACI (passthrough).

start.description: UTF-16 code-unit offset into the caller's body.

length.description: UTF-16 code-unit length of the mentioned range.

textStyle.description: Contract revision 1.69 (§4.62): optional text-formatting ranges over the body — the official bodyRanges write face. Unlike mentions, the list fails closed: an unknown style or more than 64 entries answer INVALID_REQUEST (the sender's own ranges are caller-authored, never dropped or truncated), and no body-bounds check runs (the official parseTextStyles validates none — the caller owns its offsets). A retry rebuilds the send without the ranges (§4.29 mentions deviation).

style.description: The official TextStyle vocabulary; NONE is the internal unstyled marker and is not valid here.

start.description: UTF-16 code-unit offset into the caller's body.

length.description: UTF-16 code-unit length of the styled range.

previews.description: Outbound link preview (contract §5.10 v1.26; date since 1.137 §4.126). At most one preview is used — only the first entry rides upstream (the signal-cli one-preview discipline); extras are ignored and absence of the key means no preview. The entry's url must appear in the message text (a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST otherwise), and image is an RFC 2397 data:image/ URI (never a caller path). date is the card's publish stamp in epoch ms: 0 reads as absent (the official cleanLinkPreviewDate falsy posture) and rides upstream as previewDate; negative/fractional/non-integer values fail params deserialization. The pending row persists the card metadata-only (never the image bytes), and a retry rebuild restores it without the image.

url.description: Absolute http(s) url; must appear in the message text.

title.description: Preview title; at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes.

description.description: Optional preview description; at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

imageDataUri.description: Optional preview image as an RFC 2397 data:image/ URI (~1 MiB binary with base64 inflation); transit-only — never persisted connector-side.

date.description: Optional card publish stamp (epoch ms); 0 reads as absent, a positive value rides upstream as previewDate and persists on the row.

storyReplyAuthor.description: Contract revision 1.156 (§4.154): the replied-to story's author address (the story author's ACI or phone number), forwarded verbatim onto the engine send frame's storyReplyAuthor. Forwarded verbatim — the empty/shape gate and the resolvability are the engine's. Optional and independent of storyReplyTimestamp on this face: the pair discipline (both-present or both-absent) is the engine's fail-closed parse, never a connector gate.

storyReplyTimestamp.description: Contract revision 1.156 (§4.154): the replied-to story's own Signal timestamp (epoch ms), forwarded verbatim onto the engine send frame's storyReplyTimestamp. Raw JSON value by design (the 1.151 sendCallEvent timestamp posture) — the zero/negative/fractional/non-integer gate is the engine's.

messageGetByClientRequestIdParams.description: Contract 1.172 (§4.172): the read-only orphan-sweep probe — one ledger row addressed by the original send's idempotency key, answered with its settled state in the messages.list row shape (reactions, edits and the outbound quote projection attached). Zero mutation, no upstream traffic. A row the store never saw answers MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND (the original request never arrived); a row from another conversation answers INVALID_REQUEST.

messagesRetryTextParams.description: Contract 1.31 (+ 1.172 replay semantics): retry one definitively-failed outgoing text by its clientRequestId (the same idempotency key the original send used). The connector rearms the SAME pending row (status 'failed' -> 'pending') and re-dispatches the upstream send rebuilt from the persisted record — a retry never mints a new clientRequestId, so the local history keeps exactly one row per logical message (official resend behavior; the superseded-row duplication of a naive new-id retry cannot occur). Guards: the row must be an outgoing row with a stored clientRequestId in the terminal state 'failed' — 'pending' answers RETRY_IN_FLIGHT, 'unknown' answers RETRY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (its wire outcome was never settled, so a blind resend could double-deliver; the host must never auto-resend an unknown outcome), incoming/system rows and rows without a clientRequestId answer INVALID_REQUEST, a missing row or conversation answers MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND / CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND. Contract 1.172 (§4.172) idempotent replay: a retry addressed at a row whose original send already completed (status 'sent'/'delivered'/'read') is NOT refused — it answers the persisted terminal row (same MessageRecord shape the first success answered, including the outgoing quote projection), store untouched, never re-dispatched. Replay precedes the rebuild guards, so a completed attachment send replays too; only a FAILED row's rebuild keeps the guards — an attachment row answers RETRY_NOT_ALLOWED (§4.134) and an empty-text row answers INVALID_REQUEST. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the SAME MessageRecord (same row id) now 'sent', an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN leaving the row 'unknown', a definite upstream error answers UPSTREAM_ERROR with the row back in 'failed'. The read-only probe messages.getByClientRequestId (contract 1.172) answers the same ledger row's settled state without any mutation.

contactsListParams.description: Read lane over the local contacts cache (§6.5: never calls upstream); ordered by (kind, peerKey), page-bounded, cursor-resumable. Contract 1.44 (§4.43): every result row carries isSelf (always-serialized boolean): true exactly for the kind='contact' entry whose peerKey equals the account's own number — the Note to Self entry the 1.43 contacts sync keeps in the cache, so the desktop can render the localized Note to Self title/avatar in the compose list. Number-based by the §4.24 boundary (the own ACI is not queryable upstream, a UUID-keyed row cannot be marked); group rows are never self. The self row's title stays raw material (the account's own profile name); the desktop localizes the presentation from isSelf — the connector ships no copy. Read-time derivation over the row plus the account record: nothing is stored on the cache row, contacts.sync is unchanged, and the page cursor key stays (kind, peerKey). Contract 1.60 (§4.52): every result row carries isTerminated (plain bool, present only when true — absent on false, pre-1.60 hosts read byte-identical rows): the row's own §4.50 appendix termination marker for kind='group' entries; direct rows and pre-1.53 sync rows answer absent/false. The compose face and the conversation face cannot disagree about the same group. Contract 1.146 (§4.144): every direct result row additively carries serviceId (absent-key, skip when None) derived at read time through the §4.129 family the conversation summaries run — a UUID-shaped peer key answers verbatim, a phone-keyed row (either spelling) maps through the most recent ingest-written peer_identities mapping, an unresolved key and every group row answer absent (no identifier invented); the compose/call surfaces read the same identity the summaries carry, and pre-1.146 hosts read byte-identical rows.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter over title and peerKey; read-only over the local cache.

messagesEditParams.description: Edit one message the linked account itself sent (contract 1.15; upstream face migrated to the engine's native editMessage wire method in contract 1.105 — the host params and result are unchanged). Only a local outgoing row in the terminal state 'sent' qualifies: its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp the edit targets via the engine's targetTimestamp parameter; pending/failed/unknown rows carry no protocol identity and answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. Dispatches the engine editMessage method (the official edit send face: Content.editMessage{targetSentTimestamp, dataMessage} — a true upstream edit, not a new message); the connector enforces no local edit window — a late edit answers the upstream rejection (UPSTREAM_ERROR). On confirmed success the updated MessageRecord is returned (body replaced, editedAt set, status unchanged); when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined the answer is SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and the local row is unchanged; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector. Targeting is by conversationId only — the target must already exist in the local history. clientRequestId is accepted for host correlation but the connector does not persist it for edits.

text.description: New message body; bounds identical to messages.sendText.

clientRequestId.description: Optional host correlation id; validated but not persisted.

messagesRemoteDeleteParams.description: Remotely delete (Delete for everyone) one message the linked account itself sent. Only a local outgoing row in the terminal state 'sent' qualifies: its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp addressed by the delete; pending/failed/unknown rows carry no protocol identity and answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. Best effort upstream semantics (24h window, quoted/replying messages are not removed). Targeting is by conversationId only — the target must already exist in the local history. The result is {status: 'deleted'} when signal-cli confirmed the delete, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesSendReactionParams.description: Send or remove a reaction to one message that already exists in the local history. Targeting is by conversationId only. A local outgoing row qualifies in the terminal state 'sent' (its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp); an incoming row carries the envelope timestamp, so both directions are addressable. The target author follows the row direction: the linked account's own number for outgoing rows, the conversation peer for incoming rows. Rows without a resolvable protocol identity (missing, pending/failed/unknown outgoing, system) answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND; a group incoming row persists only a local sender hash, so its author is not resolvable and the request fails with a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when signal-cli confirmed the reaction, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. remove=true removes a previously sent reaction (upstream best effort).

emoji.description: The reaction; a single unicode grapheme cluster of at most 32 UTF-8 bytes, mirroring the pinned signal-cli requirement.

remove.description: True removes a previously sent reaction; the emoji must still identify the reaction to remove.

messagesSendPinMessageParams.description: Pin one message that already exists in the local history (contract revision 1.33). Since the multi-pin queue face (diff-C #54) the official model applies — up to 3 pins per conversation (getPinnedMessagesLimit), receiver-side replace-earliest at the cap — and every summary row projects the full queue as the additive pinnedMessages array (pinned_at ASC) beside the legacy newest-pin pinnedMessage key. Addressing follows the messages.sendReaction model: a local outgoing row qualifies in the terminal state 'sent' (its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp); an incoming direct row carries the envelope timestamp; the target author follows the row direction (the linked account's own number for outgoing rows, the conversation peer for incoming direct rows). Rows without a resolvable protocol identity (missing, pending/failed/unknown outgoing, system, group incoming — only a local sender hash is persisted) fail closed: MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND or a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. Groups address the engine groupId form, direct chats the recipient array. pinDurationSeconds is the optional timed-pin duration: absent or null is the official forever pin, and a value outside 0..4294967295 fails closed with INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the pin, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

pinDurationSeconds.description: Optional timed-pin duration in seconds; absent or null means the pin never expires.

messagesSendUnpinMessageParams.description: Unpin one message that already exists in the local history (contract revision 1.33). Same addressing as messages.sendPinMessage, with no duration: the official unpinMessage carries only the target identity. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the unpin, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesSendAdminDeleteParams.description: Remove one message from a group conversation as a group admin (contract revision 1.33; the official deleted-by-admin tombstone). Direct chats have no admin concept and answer INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. Same addressing as messages.sendPinMessage; admin eligibility is not pre-checked — the server is the authority and rejects non-admin attempts, which surface as the upstream error. A group incoming row persists only a local sender hash, so its author is not resolvable and the request fails with a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the removal, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesMarkReadParams.description: Send the upstream read receipt for messages the peers authored (contract revision 1.34; official sendReceipts per-author fan-out, one engine sendReadReceipt per author with that author's timestamps, the engine chunking 100 per envelope). messageIds is optional: absent means every receipt-eligible incoming row of the conversation in ascending sentAt order, both forms bounded at 512 (an explicit list beyond 512 is truncated, not rejected). Only incoming rows qualify — outgoing and system rows are skipped; rows whose author cannot be resolved from local data (group rows carry only a local sender hash) are skipped from the fan-out, not an error. The connector does not persist our own read state (the desktop owns its unread state), so the absent form may re-receipt rows the desktop already marked — duplicates are protocol-idempotent for the peer. The result is {status: 'sent'} when every per-author upstream call confirmed, or {status: 'unknown'} when any failed (including an indeterminate outcome); a receipt failure never fails the request and 'unknown' is never retried automatically. Zero eligible rows is a trivial {status: 'sent'} no-op. Stopgap (§4.119, connector-internal, no wire change): the absent form selects only rows newer than seven days — the upstream rejects stale receipt timestamps, so older rows drop out of the selection; the explicit messageIds form is unfiltered.

messageIds.description: Optional explicit selection; only incoming rows of this conversation qualify, others are skipped.

messagesMarkViewedParams.description: Send the upstream viewed receipt (contract revision 1.34): identical addressing, selection bounds, per-author fan-out, and {status: sent|unknown} aggregation as messages.markRead, with the engine sendViewedReceipt upstream face. The selected incoming rows also take their first local viewedAt stamp (contract 1.94, §4.77 — the official readStatus === Viewed: this device played it) before the fan-out; the stamp is the request's own local effect, lands even when the group list is empty (group conversations stamp without an upstream receipt), survives an upstream failure, and never re-stamps. Stopgap (§4.119, connector-internal, no wire change): the absent form selects only rows newer than seven days and rows with no viewedAt stamp yet — the first stamp is the resupply boundary, so a row already played here is never re-sent (the official never-re-send-a-read-message posture); the explicit messageIds form is unfiltered.

messageIds.description: Optional explicit selection; only incoming rows of this conversation qualify, others are skipped.

messagesSyncReadParams.description: Send the read SELF-SYNC for messages the peers authored (contract revision 1.108, §4.89): the engine markRead face — SyncMessage.read to the account's own devices — so the account's other linked phones/desktops converge the read state. The channel is independent of the peer receipt (messages.markRead's sendReadReceipt face) and is NOT gated by the account's readReceipts configuration flag. Addressing, selection bounds (512 cap, truncation not rejection), direct-conversation author resolution, receipt-class {status: sent|unknown} aggregation, and the never-retry degradation are identical to messages.markRead; only the upstream face and its entry shape differ (the engine carries {sender, timestamp} per entry and chunks 100 per envelope internally). Zero eligible rows is a trivial {status: 'sent'} no-op; zero local writes (the desktop owns its read state). Stopgap (§4.119, connector-internal, no wire change): the absent form selects only rows newer than seven days (the §4.29 stopgap filters ride the one shared selection path).

messageIds.description: Optional explicit selection; only incoming rows of this conversation qualify, others are skipped.

messagesSyncViewedParams.description: Send the viewed SELF-SYNC (contract revision 1.108, §4.89): identical addressing, selection bounds, and receipt-class aggregation as messages.syncRead, with the engine markViewed face (SyncMessage.viewed to the account's own devices). The selected incoming rows also take their first local viewedAt stamp (contract 1.94, §4.77 — this device played it) before the sync; the stamp is the request's own local effect, lands even when the selection is empty, survives an upstream failure, and never re-stamps. Stopgap (§4.119, connector-internal, no wire change): the absent form selects only rows newer than seven days and rows with no viewedAt stamp yet (the §4.29 stopgap filters ride the one shared selection path).

messageIds.description: Optional explicit selection; only incoming rows of this conversation qualify, others are skipped.

messagesDeleteForMeEntry.description: One delete-for-me entry (the official toAddressableMessage shape): the author string (service id or e164) and the message's sent timestamp, both forwarded verbatim — the phone-side row lookup keys on the exact strings, so the connector never re-derives either.

author.description: The message's author as the desktop addressed it: a service-id string or an e164 number, forwarded verbatim.

timestamp.description: The message's sent timestamp (epoch ms); 0 is refused.

messagesDeleteForMeParams.description: Send the conversation-level delete-for-me upstream leg (contract revision 1.118, §4.99, capability delete-for-me): the engine deleteForMeConversation face — the official deleteConversation sync (SendMessage.preload.ts getDeleteForMeSyncMessage) the desktop fires when a conversation is cleared, so the account's other linked devices converge their copies too. Two arms by grammar: localOnly absent/false is the full-clear arm — mostRecentMessages is required and carries 1..=5 {author, timestamp} entries (the official slice(0, 5) mirror; a larger list answers INVALID_REQUEST — a destructive intent is never silently truncated), with the optional mostRecentNonExpiringMessages companion ≤5 (the official areAnyDisappearing companion); localOnly true is the local-only arm — mostRecent* must be absent/empty (the official local-only branch has no message position), the other devices only clear their local rows. kind must be 'contact' or 'group' (the official getConversationIdentifier refuses non-GV2 groups; legacyGroup answers INVALID_REQUEST); the conversation resolves through the local row to the upstream reference the engine's toConversationIdentifier shape carries. Entries forward verbatim. Send lane, account-scoped mutating; receipt-class {status: sent|unknown}: any engine call failure — including the pre-flight refusal — degrades to unknown and is never retried (the sync message may already ride the self-send lane). Zero local writes: the §4.83 message.deleteForMe receive mirror stays the inbound channel; this face is the outbound leg only (the §4.89 syncRead zero-local-write discipline).

kind.description: The conversation family the engine's toConversationIdentifier shape carries.

localOnly.description: true = the local-only arm (no entries allowed); absent/false = the full-clear arm (entries required).

mostRecentMessages.description: The full-clear arm's message entries (the official getMostRecentAddressableMessages().slice(0, 5) mirror; 1..=5).

mostRecentNonExpiringMessages.description: Optional companion list for conversations with disappearing messages (the official areAnyDisappearing companion; ≤5).

messagesSendViewOnceOpenParams.description: Forward the official view-once open notification (contract revision 1.38): the engine sendViewOnceOpen {account, senderAci, timestamp} face verbatim. Bare passthrough — the desktop flow does not call this directly (messages.markViewOnceOpened orchestrates both legs of the official order); result is receipt-class {status: sent|unknown} and failures degrade to unknown without retry.

timestamp.description: The viewed message's upstream timestamp (ms); 0 carries the official unknown-marker semantics.

messagesMarkViewOnceOpenedParams.description: Burn a viewed view-once message (contract revision 1.38): erase the row body bytes and the connector-owned media files, close open media handles, downgrade the row projection to the viewed placeholder, emit message.viewOnceOpened once, then best-effort orchestrate the official upstream pair (sendViewedReceipt to the author, then sendViewOnceOpen) under receipt-class discipline — failures degrade and are never retried, the burn and the event are unaffected. The desktop's single trigger point for the view-once flow; calling messages.markViewed / messages.sendViewOnceOpen separately is unnecessary (protocol-idempotent if it happens).

messagesReportSpamParams.description: Report conversation messages to the Signal anti-spam pipeline (contract revision 1.49, §4.48, capability report-spam): the engine reportSpam face verbatim — POST v1/messages/report/{senderAci}/{serverGuid} per entry, the server-assigned GUID resolved from the message rows the receive envelopes persisted (schema v17 persistence). The desktop never sees or carries a server GUID. Per-id failures are honest and partial: an id with no row, a NULL-GUID row (pre-1.49 rows or envelopes without the key), or a server rejection enters failures as {messageId, code?} (code = the server's HTTP status when it answered, absent on transport failures) while the rest of the batch still reports; the whole request fails only when the engine reports every GUID rejected (REPORT_SPAM_FAILED, retryable=false). Group conversations answer INVALID_REQUEST (the face reports individual senders; v1 exposes no per-sender selection); a direct peer whose ACI is not resolvable from local data answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. Zero local writes; the result is the engine projection {reported, failures} verbatim.

conversationId.description: The conversation the messages belong to; direct conversations only (groups answer INVALID_REQUEST).

items.description: A conversation message row id; unresolvable ids fail individually into failures.

messageIds.description: The rows to report; each must belong to this conversation.

messagesAttachmentsOpenParams.description: Open a chunked stream for one already-downloaded attachment (ADR 0004, contract revision 1.17). The (accountId, conversationId, messageId) triple resolves against the store before any file is touched — a bogus conversation or message answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND / MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. The attachmentId must be a bare file name (the id field of the received message's attachment metadata): any id containing '/' or '\\', or any id that resolves to '' / '.' / '..' under the upstream sanitizeId transform ([^A-Za-z0-9_.-] replaced by '_'), answers INVALID_REQUEST before the filesystem is touched, so a hostile id cannot path-traverse. A file signal-cli has not downloaded — or that the media governor already deleted — answers UPSTREAM_ERROR; the two are deliberately indistinguishable. Without the launcher-level --media-ingest opt-in every media method answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. The response is {mediaHandle, sizeBytes, chunkBytes}: mediaHandle is an unguessable 128-bit token bound to this resolved tuple (300 s TTL, at most 8 live handles per account, released early by messages.attachments.closeHandle), sizeBytes is the locally measured file size, and chunkBytes is the raw chunk size (262144) every readChunk offset advances by.

attachmentId.description: The upstream attachment id from the received message's attachment metadata; a bare file name, never a path.

messagesAttachmentsReadChunkParams.description: Read the next chunk of a stream opened with messages.attachments.open (ADR 0004). Offsets are strictly sequential — offset must equal the number of bytes already delivered on this handle — so a handle can never become a random-access scan oracle; any other offset answers INVALID_REQUEST. The response is {dataBase64, sizeBytes, eof}: sizeBytes counts this chunk's raw bytes (at most chunkBytes = 262144; dataBase64 is its padded standard base64, at most 4 * ceil(262144 / 3) = 349528 characters, bounded and far inside the 160 MiB host frame budget) and eof terminates the caller's read loop. A closed, expired, or unknown handle answers INVALID_REQUEST; a file truncated under the stream (media governor pass) terminates with a short chunk and eof; a file that vanished entirely answers UPSTREAM_ERROR.

offset.description: Must equal the bytes already read on this handle; 0 for the first read.

messagesAttachmentsCloseHandleParams.description: Release a media stream before its 300 s TTL (ADR 0004). Idempotent: the response is {released}, false when the handle was already gone (expired or closed earlier). Handles are also released when their account's local data is deleted; the TTL backstops every other kind of abandonment.

messagesSendAttachmentEntry.description: One plural-form attachment (contract revision 1.66): the §4.12 singular budget family per entry — standard padded base64 whose decoded size must equal sizeBytes (1..104857600 bytes), optional filename (1..128 bytes, no path separators or control characters) and optional contentType (type/subtype). No per-entry voice flag: the ;voice=true data-URI parameter is a singular-form face only. blurHash (contract revision 1.137, §4.127) is the per-entry blur placeholder: 1..128 characters, shipped verbatim to the pending row's descriptor, never decoded (the receive face's own bound — one constant, both directions). gif (contract revision 1.149, §4.147) is the per-entry GIF marker: true appends the ;gif=true data-URI parameter — shipped verbatim, the connector never interprets it; the engine maps it to the official Flags.GIF=8 bit (the receive side has projected isGif since contract 1.107) — and the entry's pending descriptor records isGif. No contentType gate: GIF-ness is a stated flag, never a media-type sniff (the official Tenor GIF is often a video/mp4 carrier).

dataBase64.description: Standard padded base64 of the attachment bytes; decoded size must equal sizeBytes.

sizeBytes.description: Declared raw size of this entry; verified against the decoded payload before anything is sent. The entries' combined total stays within the 100 MiB message budget.

filename.description: Optional display filename for the data URI; path separators and control characters are rejected.

contentType.description: Optional RFC 2045 media type 'type/subtype'; defaults to application/octet-stream.

blurHash.description: Optional blur placeholder (contract revision 1.137, §4.127): 1..128 characters, shipped verbatim onto the row descriptor for the sender's own bubble; never decoded or charset-checked. The upstream data-URI attachment channel carries no blurHash key, so upstream recipients compute their own.

gif.description: Optional GIF marker (contract revision 1.149, §4.147): true appends the ;gif=true data-URI parameter for this entry — shipped verbatim, the connector never interprets it (the engine maps it to the official Flags.GIF=8 bit) — and the entry's pending descriptor records isGif so the sender's own bubble renders the GIF UI from the first tick. No contentType gate: GIF-ness is a stated flag, never a media-type sniff.

messagesSendAttachmentParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). Two mutually exclusive payload forms (contract revision 1.66): the singular §4.12 form — dataBase64 is standard padded base64 whose decoded size must equal sizeBytes (1..104857600 bytes, the official Signal attachment ceiling), optional filename (1..128 bytes, no path separators or control characters) and contentType (type/subtype) become data-URI parameters; or the plural §4.59 form — attachments is an array of 1..32 entries (the upstream per-message ceiling), each carrying its own dataBase64/sizeBytes/filename/contentType, and the combined raw payload stays within the same 100 MiB message budget so one request still fits one host frame (the official forward face: one forwarded multi-attachment message is one upstream message). Both forms re-encode payloads as RFC 2397 data URIs for the upstream send call and never persist attachment bytes. The forms are never mixed: any singular key beside the attachments array (or a singular send missing dataBase64/sizeBytes) is INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists; voiceNote and viewOnce are singular-form faces and are INVALID_REQUEST on the plural form (a voice note is always a single-attachment message; view-once media is a single unadorned medium). gif (contract revision 1.149, §4.147) is the singular-form GIF marker — true appends the ;gif=true data-URI parameter, shipped verbatim and never interpreted by the connector (the engine maps it to the official Flags.GIF=8 bit; the receive side has projected isGif since contract 1.107); the plural form carries per-entry gif instead, and a top-level gif beside the array is INVALID_REQUEST. No contentType gate: GIF-ness is a stated flag, never a media-type sniff (the official Tenor GIF is often a video/mp4 carrier). text is an optional caption subject to the sendText byte bound and quoteMessageId quotes one message in the same conversation — shared by both forms. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the sent MessageRecord whose descriptor list carries one entry per attachment in order, and an indeterminate mutating outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with no automatic retry.

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

dataBase64.description: Singular form. Standard padded base64 of the attachment bytes; decoded size must equal sizeBytes. The bound is 4 * ceil(104857600 / 3) — the exact padded-base64 length for the 100 MiB ceiling. Mutually exclusive with the attachments array.

sizeBytes.description: Singular form. Declared raw attachment size; verified against the decoded payload before anything is sent. Mutually exclusive with the attachments array.

filename.description: Singular form. Optional display filename for the data URI; path separators and control characters are rejected. Mutually exclusive with the attachments array.

contentType.description: Singular form. Optional RFC 2045 media type 'type/subtype'; defaults to application/octet-stream. Mutually exclusive with the attachments array.

blurHash.description: Singular form. Optional blur placeholder (contract revision 1.137, §4.127): 1..128 characters, shipped verbatim onto the pending row's descriptor for the sender's own bubble; never decoded or charset-checked (the receive face's own bound — one constant, both directions). Mutually exclusive with the attachments array: the plural form carries per-entry blurHash instead.

attachments.description: Plural form (contract revision 1.66): one upstream message carries every entry, the official multi-attachment forward shape. 1..32 entries; the entries' combined sizeBytes stays within the 100 MiB message budget. Mutually exclusive with the singular dataBase64/sizeBytes/filename/contentType/blurHash keys, and with voiceNote/viewOnce/gif (the plural face carries per-entry gif instead, contract revision 1.149).

text.description: Optional caption; the service authoritatively enforces at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes. Message-level: one caption for the whole send, both forms.

voiceNote.description: Send the attachment as a voice note (contract revision 1.35): the data URI gains ;voice=true (engine maps it to the official VOICE_MESSAGE flag — the exact wire shape the official desktop recorder emits) and the sent descriptor records isVoiceNote. Requires contentType audio/*; anything else is INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists. Singular form only: INVALID_REQUEST on the plural attachments array.

viewOnce.description: Send the attachment as a view-once message (contract revision 1.38): the upstream send carries viewOnce=true and the sent row's rich record carries viewOnce so the sender's bubble renders the burn UI across restarts. Requires contentType image/* or video/*, an empty caption, no quoteMessageId, and no voiceNote; any violation is INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists. Singular form only: INVALID_REQUEST on the plural attachments array.

gif.description: Send the attachment as a GIF (contract revision 1.149, §4.147): the data URI gains ;gif=true — shipped verbatim, the connector never interprets it; the engine maps it to the official Flags.GIF=8 bit (the receive side has projected isGif since contract 1.107) — and the sent descriptor records isGif so the sender's own bubble renders the GIF UI from the first tick. No contentType gate: GIF-ness is a stated flag, never a media-type sniff (the official Tenor GIF is often a video/mp4 carrier). Singular form only: the plural attachments array carries per-entry gif instead, and a top-level gif beside the array is INVALID_REQUEST.

messagesSendStickerParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). Sends one sticker (contract revision 1.35, mirroring the official sendStickerMessage face): packId is the official hex pack id (even length, 1-64 characters), packKey the standard-base64 pack key (1-128 characters), stickerId the pack-local id, emoji an optional ≤32-character label. image follows the messages.attachments.send budget family (dataBase64 standard padded base64, decoded size must equal sizeBytes, 1..104857600 bytes) with one sticker-specific rule: contentType must be image/* (the official client sniffs image MIME and refuses video/text). The upstream send carries only the sticker object — no message body, no regular attachments. The optional quoteMessageId (contract revision 1.37, §4.35) quotes one message in the same conversation: one upstream send carries the sticker object and the quote identity together (the official StagedStickerReply shape); settlement discipline is unchanged. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the sent MessageRecord whose descriptor records the sticker image plus the pack identity, and an indeterminate mutating outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with no automatic retry.

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

quoteMessageId.description: Optional message to quote (contract revision 1.37, §4.35): resolves through the same ladder as messages.sendText — MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id, INVALID_REQUEST when the quoted author is not resolvable — and the upstream send carries quoteTimestamp/quoteAuthor beside the sticker object (the official StagedStickerReply shape). Absent means an unquoted sticker (the 1.35 behavior).

packId.description: Sticker pack id as the official client serializes it: hex, even length (each byte two hex chars), 1-64 characters; passed through verbatim after shape validation.

packKey.description: Sticker pack key in standard base64 (Bytes.fromBase64 convention), 1-128 characters; passed through verbatim after shape validation.

emoji.description: Optional emoji label for the sticker, at most 32 characters.

dataBase64.description: Standard padded base64 of the sticker image bytes; decoded size must equal sizeBytes. The bound is 4 * ceil(104857600 / 3) — the exact padded-base64 length for the 100 MiB ceiling.

sizeBytes.description: Declared raw image size; verified against the decoded payload before anything is sent.

contentType.description: RFC 2045 media type 'type/subtype'; must be image/* (the official client sniffs image MIME and refuses video/text).

width.description: Optional display width, passed through as official AttachmentPointer display metadata.

height.description: Optional display height, passed through as official AttachmentPointer display metadata.

stickerPackManifestParams.description: Fetch one sticker pack's manifest (contract revision 1.36, §4.32): the engine performs the anonymous CDN GET and the official decrypt pipeline (WebAPI.preload.ts fetch, Crypto.node.ts HKDF 'Sticker Pack' → AES-256-CBC+HMAC) — the connector never touches key material beyond passing packKey through, and never persists either field. packId is exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid — stricter than the 1.35 send projection's ≤64 on purpose); packKey is standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes. Read lane, no account context, no local state. Structured engine errors: STICKER_PACK_KEY_INVALID / STICKER_PACK_FETCH_FAILED / STICKER_PACK_MALFORMED.

packId.description: Sticker pack id, exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid).

packKey.description: Standard padded base64 of the 32-byte pack key: exactly 44 characters (11 base64 groups, one '=' pad — the only padded encoding whose decode is exactly 32 bytes).

stickerPackImageParams.description: Fetch one sticker's decrypted bytes (contract revision 1.36, §4.32): same pack identity rules as stickerPacks.getManifest plus the pack-local stickerId. The result is {dataBase64, contentType, size} — the decrypted image as standard base64 (≤ 409600 chars: the official 300 KB CDN ceiling plus base64 expansion), its media type, and the decoded byte count. The bytes exist only inside the engine and the response; nothing is persisted. Structured engine errors: the manifest family plus STICKER_IMAGE_TOO_LARGE.

packId.description: Sticker pack id, exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid).

packKey.description: Standard padded base64 of the 32-byte pack key: exactly 44 characters.

conversationsGetBlockedParams.description: Read the account's blocked conversations (contract revision 1.46, §4.45, capability blocked-conversations): the engine reads the official Storage Service records' blocked bits (per-conversation Contact/GroupV1/GroupV2 records, not the account record) and the result projects {blocked: [{conversationId, kind, blockedAtTimestampMs?}]} in storage order — the same entry shape and kind enum as the §4.33 pinned face, capped at 256 entries (KT bound, overflow truncated, entries missing identity or kind drop). Since contract revision 1.119 (§4.100, the engine's 窗D B7 read-projection) each entry additively carries blockedAtTimestampMs when the record holds a positive stamp (the official ContactRecord.blockedAtTimestamp/GroupV2Record.blockedAtTimestamp bits): 0 is the official unknown and stays absent, and GroupV1 records never carry the key (the StorageService proto has no such field for GV1). Read lane; the connector persists nothing — the cloud record plus the desktop's own cache is the whole story. There is no write counterpart on this face (the write leg is conversations.setBlocked).

conversationsGetAvatarParams.description: Download one conversation's avatar (contract revision 1.48, §4.47, capability avatar-fetch; engine alignment batch ③a): the engine resolves the conversation reference by shape — an ACI/PNI ServiceId UUID goes straight to the profile face, a phone-number text reverse-resolves through the account's contacts, a 32-byte standard-base64 group master key is the listGroups id form — downloads the encrypted avatar and decrypts it (presage profile/group faces), sniffs the MIME from the magic bytes, and answers {dataUri, byteSize}. The connector resolves the local conversation row first (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call) and forwards the row's peer reference. The result face: dataUri is a data:<mime>;base64, URI (unrecognized magic answers data:application/octet-stream;base64,) whose coarse bound is the engine's 10 MiB decoded cap plus base64 expansion — ≤ 13,981,080 chars, the §4.45 upload schema margin reused as the result guard; this schema length is the coarse envelope, the code enforces the precise decoded budget (decode + byteSize cross-check) and a violation is a protocol error. Read lane, non-mutating; nothing persists — the bytes exist only inside the engine and the response, and neither the bytes nor the URI reach a log line. Structured engine errors: AVATAR_UNAVAILABLE (the honest no-avatar: peer/group has none, profile key never synced, server 403/404 — retryable=false), AVATAR_FETCH_FAILED (network/download/decrypt — retryable=true), AVATAR_TOO_LARGE (beyond the engine's 10 MiB decoded cap — retryable=false); a parameter face the local ladder cannot reach (unknown conversation shape, unregistered account) answers the engine -32603, folded into UPSTREAM_ERROR.
