conversationId.description: The conversation to fetch the avatar for; resolved against the account before any upstream call. The engine classifies the reference shape itself (ServiceId UUID / phone number / 32-byte base64 group master key).

conversationsSetBlockedParams.description: Block or unblock one conversation (contract revision 1.48, §4.47, capability blocked-write; engine alignment batch ③a): the engine writes the official storage record's blocked bit with the official storageRecordOps semantics — the first block stamps the engine time, an already-blocked record is idempotent and never rewrites another device's timestamp, unblock clears it — then answers the post-write blocked list {blocked: [{conversationId, kind}]}, the §4.45 conversations.getBlocked result face verbatim (storage order, capped at 256 entries, entries missing identity or kind drop). The connector resolves the local conversation row first (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call) and forwards the resolved peer reference and kind. Blocking never deletes the conversation or its messages (the official desktop behaves the same). Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: CONVERSATION_NOT_RESOLVED (the cloud reference does not resolve — retryable=false) and the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable); no new codes on this face.

conversationId.description: The conversation to block or unblock; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

kind.description: The upstream conversation reference taxonomy: direct chat, GroupsV2 group, or GroupsV1 legacy group.

blocked.description: true blocks the conversation, false unblocks it. Required — there is no toggle form.

conversationsGetStateParams.description: Read one conversation's cloud state bits (contract revision 1.116, §4.97, capability conversation-state): the engine reads the official Storage Service record's three bits — mutedUntilTimestamp (epoch ms; 0 = not muted), archived, markedUnread — off the record family the kind names (Contact / GroupV1 / GroupV2) and answers {mutedUntilTimestamp, archived, markedUnread}, all three keys always present (0/false = unset bit; a record the cloud has not materialized reads as the all-default projection — the honest idempotent read). The connector resolves the local conversation row first (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call) and forwards the resolved peer reference and kind. Structured engine errors: CONVERSATION_NOT_RESOLVED (the reference does not resolve in the engine's storage taxonomy — retryable=false) and the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable); a parameter face the local ladder cannot reach (unregistered account) folds into UPSTREAM_ERROR (retryable=false — the deterministic-refusal discipline). Read lane; the connector persists nothing — the cloud record plus the desktop's own cache is the whole story.

conversationId.description: The conversation to read; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

kind.description: The upstream conversation reference taxonomy: direct chat, GroupsV2 group, or GroupsV1 legacy group — the record family the engine reads.

conversationsSaveDraftParams.description: Stamp one conversation's draft clock (contract revision 1.138, §4.130): the connector stores the official DraftRepository record's timestamp alone — draft text never crosses this wire (the desktop keeps it in its own safeStorage; the connector is body-blind by construction). The face is local state with no engine and no upstream (the history.importRetry lane shape): send lane, account-scoped mutating — the same-account write mutex and delete barrier apply through the host acquire — and the refreshed summary rides conversation.changed, so every window sees the new draft clock without a re-read. The conversation row resolves first (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any write); re-saving the same conversation replaces its stamp. draftTimestamp is the connector-clock epoch millisecond the desktop wants the list to sort/label the draft by; it must be positive (0 is the absent fold — clearing is conversations.clearDraft's explicit job, a 0 stamp answers INVALID_REQUEST). Result is {status: 'saved'}.

conversationId.description: The conversation to stamp; resolved against the account before any write.

draftTimestamp.description: The draft's clock (epoch ms, positive): the only draft material the connector holds. Replace-on-save, per conversation.

conversationsClearDraftParams.description: Clear one conversation's draft clock (contract revision 1.138, §4.130): the stamp is the whole draft record, so the clear is the save's inverse on the same local lane — no engine, no upstream, send lane, account-scoped mutating, and the refreshed summary rides conversation.changed. The conversation row resolves first (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any write); the face is idempotent — a conversation with no stored draft still answers {status: 'cleared'} (a replay stays silent).

conversationId.description: The conversation to clear; resolved against the account before any write.

conversationsSetStateParams.description: Write one conversation's cloud state bits (contract revision 1.116, §4.97, capability conversation-state): the engine reads the official Storage Service record, flips only the flags the caller sent (absent = no write intent for that bit — the official partial-write grammar; the flag values carry no tri-state of their own), encodes the record back field-preserving (decode→mutate→encode keeps every other byte of the record, the official toModelRecorder semantics), and answers the post-write projection {mutedUntilTimestamp, archived, markedUnread} — the §4.97 getState result face verbatim. At least one flag is required: an empty intent answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call (there is no toggle-to-nothing form). The connector resolves the local conversation row first (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call) and forwards the resolved peer reference, kind, and the present flags only. The set is idempotent cloud-side: re-sending an already-satisfied intent is a no-op write that answers the same projection. mutedUntilTimestamp is epoch ms (0 clears the mute). Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Zero local writes: the projection converges through the desktop's own cache and later reads. Structured engine errors: CONVERSATION_NOT_RESOLVED (retryable=false) and the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable); a bare engine -32603 (the parameter face the typed ladder cannot produce) folds into UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false; no new codes on this face.

conversationId.description: The conversation to write; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

kind.description: The upstream conversation reference taxonomy: direct chat, GroupsV2 group, or GroupsV1 legacy group — the record family the engine writes.

mutedUntilTimestamp.description: Write the mute expiry (epoch ms); 0 clears the mute. Absent = leave the current value untouched.

archived.description: Write the archive bit. Absent = leave the current value untouched.

markedUnread.description: Write the marked-unread bit. Absent = leave the current value untouched.

callsSendSignalParams.description: Forward one outbound call-signaling frame (contract revision 1.82, §4.49, capability call-signaling): the connector shape-gates the envelope — type against the RingRTC 1:1 frame-family enum, callId a positive integer (u32 face, the legacy frames' id address space), payload mandatory (non-empty, ≤ 3,145,728 chars, the coarse envelope of the same budget the receive face enforces) for the modern faces offer/answer/ice and optional (absent) for the legacy busy/hangup family — the official proto bare frames CallMessage{busy{id}} / CallMessage{hangup{...}} carry no opaque field (RingRTC 2.72.1 emits them opaque-less, verified in the P1 device experiment), so a payload-less busy/hangup routes the engine sendCallMessage legacy face instead of inventing bytes — resolves the local conversation row (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call) and routes by the conversation kind (1.82, no new parameter — the connector already holds the kind): a direct conversation forwards byte-for-byte as the engine's {account, recipient, data|legacy} 1:1 face; a group conversation routes the engine group face {account, group (the master key, the same reference listGroups addresses), data, urgency} — the sender-key fan-out (send_message_to_group), the official #handleSendCallMessageToGroup → sendContentMessageToGroup landing mirrored as a pass-through — and refuses the payload-less legacy family locally (official group signaling rides the opaque envelope exclusively; callId and type gate but never travel). urgency (1.55) is the optional pass-through wake-up bit forwarded to the engine's CallMessage{opaque{urgency}} (absent = the engine's droppable default). hangupType and destinationDeviceId (contract 1.144, §4.142) are the two optional RingRTC passthrough words: hangupType rides the payload-less hangup bare frame as the engine legacy face's type (the official Hangup{id,type} family, the engine's five-word vocabulary; absent = the type-less pre-1.144 frame), and destinationDeviceId rides the 1:1 arm as the engine's directed-delivery passthrough (positive u32, 0 refused; a group conversation refuses it locally). The connector never parses, validates, or logs the signaling content: the engine owns the transport face (Content.callMessage=3, official Signal-Desktop RingRTC behavior aligned, AGPL zero-copy) and the desktop + calling sidecar's RingRTC state machine parses the frames. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier apply (the group fan-out's latency rides the same lane — a known, recorded characteristic); an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. The result {sentAt} is the engine's envelope timestamp — a send ack, not call state.

conversationId.description: The conversation the signaling addresses; resolved against the account before any upstream call. The kind decides the route (1.82): direct keeps the 1:1 recipient face, group routes the engine sender-key fan-out face.

type.description: The RingRTC 1:1 frame family the frame carries. offer/answer/ice demand payload (the RingRTC-serialized opaque material); busy/hangup may omit it (the legacy bare-frame family, engine-built from the callId) on a direct conversation — on a group conversation the payload-less legacy family refuses locally (group signaling is opaque-only). Gated for the route decision and the desktop-side logging/routing honesty; the payload itself is self-describing.

callId.description: The 1:1 call identity the RingRTC frames share (the legacy frames' id face). Positive u32; 0 is the no-call marker and is rejected.

payload.description: The opaque signaling material (RingRTC-serialized), forwarded byte-for-byte. Mandatory for offer/answer/ice; omit for a legacy busy/hangup bare frame (the engine builds CallMessage{busy{id}} / CallMessage{hangup{id}}). The connector validates the envelope shape only — never the content.

urgency.description: The optional wake-up bit (contract 1.55), forwarded to the engine's CallMessage{opaque{urgency}}. Absent = the engine's droppable default (proto: a missing urgency treats as DROPPABLE). Only meaningful with a payload (the legacy bare frames have no opaque envelope).

hangupType.description: The legacy hangup word (contract 1.144, §4.142), forwarded as the engine legacy face's type on CallMessage{hangup{id,type}} — the engine's five-word vocabulary, the same words the inbound projection emits. Legal only on a payload-less hangup bare frame: any other type, a busy frame, or a hangup carrying a payload answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. Absent = the type-less Hangup{id} the engine reads as HangupNormal, the pre-1.144 shape.

destinationDeviceId.description: The directed-delivery device id (contract 1.144, §4.142), forwarded as the engine's top-level destinationDeviceId on the 1:1 arm only (official group signaling is the sender-key fan-out with no device-directed face — a group conversation carrying it answers INVALID_REQUEST locally). Positive u32; 0 is the no-device marker and is rejected. Absent = the engine's no-write default, the pre-1.144 shape.

callsSendGroupCallUpdateParams.description: Send one group-call era update (contract revision 1.127, §4.108, capability call-signaling widened in place — no new capability bit; the official DataMessage.groupCallUpdate face, the engine sendGroupCallUpdate method): the connector resolves the local conversation row (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call) and refuses any non-group kind locally — group call signaling has no direct form, 1:1 call signaling rides calls.sendSignal. The row's peer reference is the upstream groupId and is gated locally as standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes (the group master key the engine's decode_group_id face re-gates); eraId is the mandatory non-empty RingRTC era identity string (≤256 characters). Send lane, account-scoped mutating: the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier apply; the definite success answers the explicit {"status":"sent"} (the engine's own body is empty — the update's identity is the era string itself) and an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, never retried (an era update whose delivery is unknown may already sit in the group's call state).

conversationId.description: The group conversation the update addresses; resolved against the account before any upstream call. A non-group kind answers INVALID_REQUEST.

eraId.description: The RingRTC group-call era identity string, forwarded verbatim on DataMessage.groupCallUpdate.

callsGetStateParams.description: Read the connector's call-state registry (contract revision 1.51, §4.49, capability call-signaling): account-scoped, repeatable, store-only — no engine call, no network. The honest projection: the connector is the signaling pipe between the engine's transport and the desktop + calling sidecar's RingRTC state machine; it persists no call state, so the registry reads {calls: [], projection: "connector-pipe"} — the stable face a later batch fills if the connector ever learns to register state. Read lane.

callsLinkPresentationParams.description: Produce the day's call-link auth credential presentation (contract revision 1.88, §4.73, capability call-signaling widened in place — no new capability bit; engine a3ae39b, engine jsonrpc-compat §3 calls row + §5 block). Pure material passthrough: the connector gates the shapes and resolves the account, then forwards {account, rootKey} to the engine verbatim and passes the engine's result through untouched — zero logic, zero parsing, zero logging (the credential/presentation bytes cross this process exactly once, engine → host; the connector caches nothing, persists nothing, logs nothing — the engine keeps the per-account credential cache, the relay-api-v2 §5 credentials-never-ride-host-HTTP ruling). rootKey is the RingRTC CallLinkRootKey: standard base64 decoding to exactly 16 bytes (V0) or 21 bytes (V1); the maxLength 28 is the padded-base64 wire bound of the widest legal form. A shape violation answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call (the engine re-gates fail-closed); an unregistered account or an engine-side refusal degrades per the structured ladder: CALL_CREDENTIALS_FAILED (retryable=false — server rejection, zkgroup redemption/presentation verification failure, the day's credential absent; error.data.status carries the server HTTP status verbatim when the server gave one), CALL_CREDENTIALS_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=true — network/transport). Result {presentation}: the CallLinkAuthCredentialPresentation bincode bytes, standard base64 (the desktop/calling RingRTC binding consumes the decoded bytes). Read lane, non-mutating.

rootKey.description: The call-link root key: standard (padded) base64 decoding to exactly 16 bytes (V0) or 21 bytes (V1) — the RingRTC CallLinkRootKey two-version lengths; zkgroup derives from the first 16-byte CRN. Gated locally before any upstream call; the material is never parsed, logged, or stored.

callsCreateLinkAuthParams.description: Run the call-link create-auth two-shot inside one RPC (contract revision 1.88, §4.73, capability call-signaling; engine a3ae39b, engine jsonrpc-compat §3 calls row + §5 block). Pure material passthrough: the connector gates both shapes and forwards {account, rootKey, roomId} verbatim; the engine runs POST v1/call-link/create-auth → credential redemption → presentation + public params and passes both byte strings back. The server-side POST is credential issuance with no user-visible state change, so the face stays read-only (no write lane, no SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN). rootKey gated exactly as on calls.linkPresentation; roomId is the RingRTC derive_room_id output: standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes (the HKDF-SHA256 fixed-length output; the official callers derive it from the root key, never invent it). Error ladder identical to calls.linkPresentation (CALL_CREDENTIALS_FAILED with data.status?, CALL_CREDENTIALS_UNAVAILABLE, local INVALID_REQUEST shape gates). Result {presentation, callLinkPublicParams}: the CreateCallLinkCredentialPresentation and CallLinkPublicParams bincode bytes, each standard base64 (the official createCallLink credential segment's two materials). Read lane, non-mutating.

rootKey.description: The call-link root key: standard base64 decoding to exactly 16 (V0) or 21 (V1) bytes; same gate as calls.linkPresentation.

roomId.description: The derived room id: standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes — the RingRTC derive_room_id HKDF-SHA256 fixed output. Generated by the RingRTC side (rootKey.generate/derive_room_id); the connector never derives and never stores it.

callsGroupProofParams.description: Fetch the day's group membership proof token (contract revision 1.88, §4.73, capability call-signaling; engine a3ae39b, engine jsonrpc-compat §3 calls row + §5 block). Pure material passthrough: the connector gates the group shape and forwards {account, groupId} verbatim; the engine redeems the day's AuthCredentialWithPni, presents it against the group's public params, and reads GET v2/groups/token on the storage-service host — the ExternalGroupCredential token comes back as a plain string (RingRTC setMembershipProof consumes its UTF-8 bytes). groupId is the same 32-byte group master key the listGroups/terminateGroup faces address: standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes. Error ladder identical to calls.linkPresentation: local INVALID_REQUEST shape gates, CALL_CREDENTIALS_FAILED (retryable=false; server rejection, non-membership, proto decode failure, the day's credential absent; data.status? verbatim), CALL_CREDENTIALS_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=true). Result {proof}: the token string. Read lane, non-mutating.

groupId.description: The group master key: standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes — the same reference listGroups addresses.

callsGroupMembersParams.description: Fetch the group's member cipher-text material (contract revision 1.88, §4.73, capability call-signaling; engine a3ae39b, engine jsonrpc-compat §3 calls row + §5 block). Pure material passthrough: the calls.groupProof gate and forwarding discipline verbatim; the engine reads the group state (GET v1/groups/ + its own decryption) and encrypts every member's ACI into a UuidCiphertext — the RingRTC GroupMemberInfo material for group-call endorsements. groupId gated exactly as on calls.groupProof. Error ladder identical: local INVALID_REQUEST shape gates, CALL_CREDENTIALS_FAILED (retryable=false, data.status?), CALL_CREDENTIALS_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=true). deletedAtTimestampMs.description: The tombstone timestamp for the delete-arm write (positive; 0 is refused — the engine reads 0 as no action); omit for the active arm. Exactly one of adminPasskey / deletedAtTimestampMs must be present.

groupsGetParams.description: Read-only projection (contract revision 1.9, roster added in 1.40, isTerminated added in 1.53, requestingMembers added in 1.62, pendingMembers added in 1.64, member label pair added in 1.67, linkAccess added in 1.180, announcementsOnly and the role-word admin/self marks added in 1.181, description added in 1.188) of the local contacts cache for one group: {peerKey, title, memberCount?, members?, isTerminated, linkAccess?, announcementsOnly?, description?, requestingMembers?, pendingMembers?, syncedAt}. Served from the rows written by contacts.sync — the connector never calls the upstream for the cached face, so an unsynced or departed group (the sync filters isMember=false) answers GROUP_NOT_FOUND; syncedAt lets the host judge staleness itself. members (contract 1.40, §4.39) is the bounded roster the sync captured (cap 1001, the official GroupsV2 group-size ceiling): entries carry id (the connector-wide number-before-uuid address ladder), optional uuid (only when the upstream supplied one), optional name (resolved at read time from the same account's contacts cache; absent when unknown), self (true when the entry's id is the linked account's number, or its id or uuid is the account's stored ACI — contract 1.181 folds the ACI, the engine roster id falls back to the member's ACI service-id string when the number lookup misses; absent otherwise), admin (only when the upstream marks the member: the GV2 role word ADMINISTRATOR captured since 1.181 beside the legacy isAdmin/admins reads — absent on engines without an admin face), and the member label pair labelEmoji/label (contract 1.67, §4.60: the upstream member's own label captured verbatim at sync under the server budgets emoji ≤64B / string ≤512B, over-budget or empty drops the key; absent for label-less members, engine-mode rosters, and pre-1.67 rows). Rows synced before 1.40 carry no members key. isTerminated (contract 1.53, §4.50 appendix) is the upstream JsonGroup.isTerminated flag as of the row's last sync, projected as a plain bool — false for pre-1.53 rows and engines without the flag; the receive envelope (JsonGroupInfo) exposes no terminated field, so only the next sync refreshes it and syncedAt remains the staleness signal. linkAccess (contract 1.180, §4.180) is the upstream JsonGroup.addFromInviteLink word the sync captured, projected only inside the official vocabulary — ANY (link on, joins without approval), ADMINISTRATOR (link on, admin-approval gate), UNSATISFIABLE (link off); MEMBER is not a link-join state and UNKNOWN is the engine's unparsed fallback, so both collapse to an absent key (unknown, never a lie), as do pre-1.180 rows and malformed stored values; the desktop derives the official hasGroupLink/approval states (GroupLinkManagement.dom.tsx:46-53) from it, and the next sync refreshes it like isTerminated. requestingMembers (contract 1.62, §4.53 appendix) is the one live face of this method: the same single-group upstream listGroups read the 1.58 approval fold runs against, projected to bounded entries {id (the first-wins address ladder — either identity folds), uuid?, name?}; present only when the engine answered with a non-empty requesting set, absent otherwise (the engine is stopped, the upstream face is missing, or nobody is requesting — the desktop renders no approval section). The key is deliberately NOT a sync-captured cache field: the approval truth source is the fold's own live read (the 1.58 record), and one source keeps the rendered list and the folded write set from ever disagreeing; freshness is the read call itself, which also lets the desktop's post-action refresh observe the converged list without waiting for contacts.sync. pendingMembers (contract 1.64, §4.57, capability group-invite-revoke — one capability for the read and write halves) is the same-shaped live read of the invited-but-not-yet-joined set: the same single-group listGroups read the §4.57 revoke fold runs against, projected to bounded entries {id, uuid?, name?}; present only when the engine answered a non-empty pending set, absent otherwise. The upstream face carries no inviter metadata (JsonGroupMemberAddress has no addedByUserId), so no invited-by grouping rides this face — the official PendingInvites panel groups rows by inviter, a recorded projection difference. announcementsOnly (contract 1.181, §4.181) is the upstream JsonGroup.announcementsOnly flag the sync captured verbatim, projected as an optional bool — the CompositionArea.dom.tsx:1108 `announcementsOnly && !areWeAdmin` banner gate's first half, the roster's admin/self marks answering the second; absent on pre-1.181 rows and captures without the key (unknown, never a guessed false — a legacy face without the flag keeps the key absent), and a malformed stored value drops rather than fails the read; the next sync refreshes it like every other captured flag. description (contract 1.188, §4.188) is the group description the sync captured from the engine's decrypted group state (the engine listGroups optional `description` key; the pinned signal-cli JsonGroup never set one), under the write face's own whole-value budget (4096 bytes) re-checked at read — absent on pre-1.188 rows, engines without the face, and groups with no description (the honest unsynced placeholder, never an invented empty-known state); an over-budget or malformed stored value drops rather than fails the read, and the next sync refreshes it like every other captured field. Metrics classify it as contacts; no event is emitted.

groupKey.description: The upstream group id, exactly the peerKey of the cached kind='group' contacts row.

groupsCommonParams.description: Groups in common (contract revision 1.181, §4.181): the official contact-details panel's groups-in-common answer (ConversationDetails.preload.tsx:80-100 — a direct peer's identity against every group's member list, title-sorted) served read-only from the local contacts cache the §4.39 sync captured: zero engine calls, zero writes. The target must be a direct conversation — a group conversationId answers INVALID_REQUEST (an honest shape refusal; the official face lives on the contact panel). The answer is {groups: [{peerKey, title}]}: the contact's identity set (the peer key in both phone spellings, its peer_identities ACI, and the reverse peer keys when the peer key is itself ACI-shaped) matched against each captured roster entry's id/uuid, each roster bounded to the 1001 capture cap, title-sorted like the official panel with the peerKey as the deterministic tiebreak. An empty list is the honest no-groups-in-common answer — the capture only knows what the last contacts sync saw, and each group's own syncedAt (on groups.get) remains the staleness signal. Metrics classify it as contacts; no event is emitted.

groupsUpdateParams.description: Apply one group-management change set to one group conversation (contract revision 1.45, §4.44; avatar tri-state added by contract revision 1.89; the engine write face wired by contract revision 1.115, §4.96). The change keys are individually optional and mirror the pinned signal-cli updateGroup jsonRpc surface verbatim: name (from groupName), description (from groupDescription), members (from addMembers), removeMembers, admins (from promoteAdmins), removeAdmins (from demoteAdmins), bans (from banMembers), unbans (from unbanMembers), resetLink, link (from linkState: the connector's enabled-without-approval maps to the upstream choice 'enabled'), setPermissionAddMember / setPermissionEditDetails / setPermissionSendMessages (every-member | only-admins), memberLabel, memberLabelEmoji. At least one change parameter must be present (an empty change set answers INVALID_REQUEST; resetLink=false counts as absent). An empty member array is INVALID_REQUEST — upstream reads absence as 'no change' and an explicit empty set would commit a no-delta group change broadcast. Member arrays carry at most 1001 entries (the official GroupsV2 ceiling), each 1-128 chars, forwarded verbatim (the upstream resolves and rejects unknown addresses). groupName/memberLabel 1-256 bytes, groupDescription up to 4096 bytes, memberLabelEmoji one emoji grapheme cluster (<=32 bytes). conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any upstream call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST). Group avatar (since contract 1.89, the accounts.setProfile tri-state): absent = keep, explicit null = remove, a data:image/*;base64, data URI (decoded 1..10485760 bytes) = replace — the avatar member counts toward the at-least-one-change rule, and the value rides upstream verbatim. The wired engine subset (1.115): the change set folds onto the engine's updateGroup vocabulary — groupName→title, addMembers/removeMembers verbatim, the avatar tri-state verbatim, and linkState onto the engine's addFromInviteLinkAccess word (enabled-without-approval→ANY, enabled-with-approval→ADMINISTRATOR, disabled→UNSATISFIABLE), and (contract revision 1.180, §4.180) resetLink onto the engine's inviteLinkPassword arm: the connector mints the official 16-byte CSPRNG password locally (the official client's own refreshGroupLink posture, conversations.preload.ts:4793-4795) and rides it standard base64 onto the payload — the old link dies with the old password, and (contract revision 1.188, §4.188) setPermissionSendMessages onto the engine's announcementsOnly bool (only-admins → true, every-member → false — the official modifyAnnouncementsOnly change, groups.preload.ts:895-904; both values are real write intents, lifting included; engine arm 8ea56f6 on the engine's pushed integration line — an engine build without the arm answers the plain engine refusal through the structured UPSTREAM_ERROR face). A change set naming any key outside that subset (groupDescription — the engine's updateGroup still carries no description write arm, a recorded gap; promoteAdmins/demoteAdmins, banMembers/unbanMembers, the remaining permission pair permissionAddMember/permissionEditDetails, memberLabel/memberLabelEmoji) answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) naming the offending keys after local validation — the honest whole-call refusal, never a partial application (the engine commits the set as one change broadcast). Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. A server-rejected change answers GROUP_UPDATE_FAILED (retryable=false) with data {status?} — the honest HTTP pass-through; a 409 revision race unblocks only after the caller re-reads the group state (groups.get / conversations.list), never by blind replay of the same change set. The engine's deny faces (unknown account/group, non-member) answer UPSTREAM_ERROR with retryable=false — deterministic refusals a replay cannot clear. A failed avatar upload after a landed group change answers GROUP_AVATAR_UPLOAD_FAILED (retryable=true) with data {retryable, textSaved} — the honest partial-success report. Group state converges through the receive projection: a bodyless groupInfo type=UPDATE envelope lands as a system row (rich marker isGroupUpdate) and conversation.changed carries the mirrored title.

conversationId.description: The group conversation to update; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

promoteAdmins.description: Members to promote to admin; upstream key 'admins'.

linkState.description: Group invite-link state; upstream key 'link'. The connector's enabled-without-approval maps to the upstream choice 'enabled'.

resetLink.description: Reset the group link: the connector mints a fresh official 16-byte CSPRNG link password and folds it onto the engine's inviteLinkPassword arm (contract revision 1.180, §4.180) — the old link dies with the old password. false carries no change semantics (absent).

permissionAddMember.description: Who may add members; upstream key 'setPermissionAddMember'.

permissionEditDetails.description: Who may edit group details; upstream key 'setPermissionEditDetails'.

permissionSendMessages.description: Who may send messages; upstream key 'setPermissionSendMessages'. Since contract revision 1.188 it folds onto the engine's announcementsOnly bool: only-admins is the announcements-only group, every-member lifts it.

memberLabel.description: The group's member label string; upstream key 'memberLabel'.

memberLabelEmoji.description: The group's member label emoji: exactly one unicode grapheme cluster of at most 32 UTF-8 bytes; upstream key 'memberLabelEmoji'.

avatar.description: Three states (contract revision 1.89, the accounts.setProfile tri-state): absent = keep the current group avatar; a data:image/*;base64, data URI whose decoded size is 1..10485760 bytes (10 MiB, the engine's stated avatar budget) = replace; explicit null = remove. The avatar member counts toward the at-least-one-change rule, and the connector keeps an explicit null distinct from an absent key (a dedicated deserialization type — the null is a remove, not a no-op). The maxLength is the padded-base64 encoding of the ceiling plus a fixed prefix margin — the connector enforces the decoded budget itself and answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. The value rides the wired engine face (contract 1.115) verbatim; the connector never writes a temporary file.

groupsQuitParams.description: Leave one group conversation (contract revision 1.45, §4.44, capability group-management; the engine write face wired by contract revision 1.115, §4.96): the engine's leaveGroup {account, groupId} write — the engine's method name for the upstream quit write (its face never carried a quitGroup literal). conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any upstream call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST). The upstream --delete local-data flag and the --admin last-admin handoff list are deliberately not exposed: the official client keeps the conversation as a non-member after leaving, and a last-admin quit without a handoff answers the upstream user error verbatim. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. The engine's deny faces (non-member, unknown account/group) answer UPSTREAM_ERROR with retryable=false — deterministic refusals a replay cannot clear. The local conversation row is kept (non-member state is upstream convergence, like groups.update).

conversationId.description: The group conversation to leave; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

groupsTerminateParams.description: Terminate one group conversation for every member (contract revision 1.52, §4.50, capability group-terminate): the upstream terminateGroup {account, groupId} write — the pinned 0.14.8 JSON-RPC face (TerminateGroupCommand, a JsonRpcLocalCommand) wrapping GroupHelper.terminateGroup → GroupV2Helper.terminateGroup → libsignal createTerminateGroup(). conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any upstream call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST). Upstream requires admin privileges; a non-admin answers the GroupsV2 UNAUTHORIZED face and a v1 group answers the v1-only refusal — both forward verbatim as the UPSTREAM_ERROR family, never invented locally. The action is irreversible on the Signal service: afterwards nobody can send messages or start calls in the group, and members keep read access to the existing history (official “End group” behavior anchors). The face is the pinned engine's gap and answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Zero local writes: the terminated state converges through the group-update receive projection (§4.44).

conversationId.description: The group conversation to terminate; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

groupsApproveJoinRequestsParams.description: Approve or refuse one group's pending join requests (contract revision 1.58, §4.53, capability group-join-approve): members carries the candidate member set (1-1001 entries of 1-128 characters, the §4.39 roster bounds; an empty array is refused — it carries no change upstream), approve=true approves the join requests, approve=false refuses them. The upstream write is the pinned 0.14.8 updateGroup face (GroupHelper.updateGroupV2 weaves approval into the member semantics: members entries that are requesting members ride approveJoinRequestMembers, removeMembers entries that are requesting members ride refuseJoinRequestMembers). Because those shared arrays would otherwise add or remove ordinary members, the connector folds the candidates against the engine's own requesting-members read (listGroups → JsonGroup.requestingMembers) before anything goes upstream — only candidates the engine still reports as requesting can ride the arrays, so a stale or mistaken candidate fails closed at the connector instead of adding or removing a member. A fold that empties the candidate set answers JOIN_REQUEST_NO_LONGER_PENDING (retryable — the request was resolved elsewhere); a candidate rejected upstream (non-admin) forwards verbatim as the UPSTREAM_ERROR family. conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any engine call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST, unknown answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND). The face answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Zero local writes: the roster converges through contacts.sync.

conversationId.description: The group conversation whose join requests are being decided; resolved against the account before any engine call.

members.description: The candidate member set (the members' numbers or uuids as the caller read them); duplicated entries collapse. Each entry must still be requesting membership at the engine or it drops from the write (fail closed).

approve.description: true approves the join requests (the members ride the upstream members family); false refuses them (the removeMembers family).

groupsRevokeInvitesParams.description: Revoke one group's pending invitations (contract revision 1.64, §4.57, capability group-invite-revoke): members carries the candidate member set (1-1001 entries of 1-128 characters, the §4.39 roster bounds; an empty array is refused — it carries no change upstream). The upstream write is the pinned 0.14.8 updateGroup removeMembers family (GroupHelper.updateGroupV2 discriminates three ways: entries that are pending members ride revokeInvitedMembers, entries that are full members ride the member removal, entries that are requesting members ride refuseJoinRequestMembers). Because that shared array would otherwise remove an ordinary member or refuse a join request, the connector folds the candidates against the engine's own pending-members read (listGroups → JsonGroup.pendingMembers) before anything goes upstream — only candidates the engine still reports as pending invitees can ride the array, so a stale or mistaken candidate fails closed at the connector instead of removing a member or refusing a request. A fold that empties the candidate set answers INVITE_NO_LONGER_PENDING (retryable — the invite was resolved elsewhere: another admin revoked it, the invitee joined); a candidate rejected upstream (non-admin) forwards verbatim as the UPSTREAM_ERROR family. conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any engine call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST, unknown answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND). The face answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Zero local writes: the roster converges through contacts.sync.

conversationId.description: The group conversation whose pending invitations are being revoked; resolved against the account before any engine call.

members.description: The candidate member set (the invitees' numbers or uuids as the caller read them); duplicated entries collapse. Each entry must still be a pending invitee at the engine or it drops from the write (fail closed).

groupsBuildInviteLinkParams.description: Build one group's invite link (contract revision 1.117, §4.98, capability group-invite-links; engine alignment batch P13): the engine encodes the official GroupInviteLink proto (contentsV1{groupMasterKey, inviteLinkPassword}) → standard base64 → websafe → https://signal.group/#<code> (the official buildGroupLink shape). With an explicit password the build is pure construction (the official explicit-password arm — fake/real same code path); without one the engine reads the server group state's link password, and a group that has not enabled its invite link answers GROUP_INVITE_LINK_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false, the honest not-set state). conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any engine call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST, unknown answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND). The password is single-pass material: standard base64 of 1-64 bytes (the official password is 16 bytes = 24 chars), forwarded verbatim — the engine's decode gate refuses other shapes (UPSTREAM_ERROR), the connector never re-derives it, and neither the password nor the link is logged or persisted. Read lane, non-mutating (both arms only read or construct); the result is {inviteLink}.

conversationId.description: The group conversation to build the link for; resolved against the account before any engine call — the row's peer reference is the group master key the link encodes.

password.description: Optional explicit link password, standard base64 (generate one with groups.generateInviteLinkPassword). Absent = the engine reads the group's server-side link state. Single-pass material: never logged, never persisted.

groupsParseInviteLinkParams.description: Parse one group invite link (contract revision 1.117, §4.98, capability group-invite-links): account-less pure proto decoding (the official parseGroupLink) — the engine accepts the three official URL forms (https://signal.group/#…, sgnl://signal.group/#…, sgnl://joingroup#…) and the bare invite code, restores websafe base64, decodes the GroupInviteLink proto, and answers {groupId, password} — the master key and password bytes as standard base64 (the master key is exactly 32 bytes = 44 chars). A link that fails any tolerance — empty/no code segment, bad base64, undecodable proto, missing contentsV1 (the official LINK_VERSION_ERROR family), wrong key length, empty password — answers the engine's -32603 face, folded into UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false (deterministic). Read lane; the decoded bytes are single-pass material — never logged, never persisted.

inviteLink.description: The link as the user pasted it — any official URL form or the bare invite code. The connector only bounds the string; the grammar is the engine's.

groupsPreviewViaLinkParams.description: Preview the group behind one invite link (contract revision 1.117, §4.98, capability group-invite-links; the official getPreJoinGroupInfo posture): the engine parses the link and reads the group's pre-join projection — {groupId, memberCount, revision, addFromInviteLink, approvalRequired, pendingAdminApproval, name?, description?} (the profile title/description ride only when the group carries them). Read lane, non-mutating; the connector persists nothing — the preview is the answer. The link is single-pass material. Structured engine errors: GROUP_INVITE_LINK_PREVIEW_FAILED (the server refused the pre-join read — data {status?} passes through verbatim, retryable=false), STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=true), and the bare -32603 parameter face (a malformed link) folded into UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false.

inviteLink.description: The link to preview — any official URL form or the bare invite code; the engine parses it.

groupsJoinViaLinkParams.description: Join the group behind one invite link (contract revision 1.117, §4.98, capability group-invite-links; the official joinGroupV2ViaLink posture): the engine parses the link and applies the join — the answer's status verb distinguishes the definite member add ('joined') from the approval gate's request ('requested'). Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried (the join may already have landed). A server rejection answers GROUP_UPDATE_FAILED with data {status?} verbatim (the 1.115 channel, retryable=false); STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE is retryable=true; a malformed link is the engine's -32603 face folded into UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false (refused before anything goes upstream). Zero local writes: the roster converges through contacts.sync.

inviteLink.description: The link to join through — any official URL form or the bare invite code; the engine parses it.

groupsCancelJoinRequestParams.description: Withdraw one join request (contract revision 1.117, §4.98, capability group-invite-links; the official cancelJoinRequest posture): a requester is not yet a member, so the withdrawal is addressed by the link the join went through — the same link-addressed shape as groups.joinViaLink. The definite success is {status: 'cancelled'}. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried; a server rejection answers GROUP_UPDATE_FAILED with data {status?} verbatim (retryable=false); STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE is retryable=true; a malformed link folds into UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false. Zero local writes: the roster converges through contacts.sync.

inviteLink.description: The link the join went through — any official URL form or the bare invite code; the engine parses it.

conversationId.description: The group conversation the poll rides — polls are group-conversation faces exclusively (the official desktop ships them in groups; the 1:1 create form rides a feature flag that defaults off, vote/terminate have no 1:1 form at all), so any other conversation kind answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call.

question.description: The poll question: 1..200 characters within 2048 bytes (the official PollCreateSchema content face, MAX_MESSAGE_BODY_BYTE_LENGTH).

items.description: One poll option: 1..100 characters within 2048 bytes.

allowMultiple.description: Whether the poll accepts multiple selections; optional (absent = the engine's false default, the official single-selection form).

messagesSendPollCreateParams.description: Create one poll in a group conversation (contract revision 1.125, §4.106, capability polls; the official DataMessage.pollCreate face): the content gates run locally fail-closed before any upstream call (the engine's poll faces pin the same bounds). Send lane, account-scoped mutating: the response is {"status":"sent"} on a definite success and the explicit {"status":"unknown"} on an indeterminate one — never an automatic retry. The upstream result body is empty; the poll's identity is the send timestamp the receive projection converges. Unknown account answers ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND.

conversationId.description: The group conversation carrying the poll (polls are group-conversation faces exclusively).

targetAuthor.description: The poll author the vote addresses (number or UUID; the §4.44 member-id bound).

targetTimestamp.description: The poll message's sent-at timestamp (the official z.number().int().positive()); 0 answers INVALID_REQUEST.

optionIndexes.description: The selected option indexes (the official PollVoteSchema domain 0..9, at most 10 entries); an empty array is the legal clear-vote action.

voteCount.description: The multi-ballot count; optional (absent = the engine's 1 default).

messagesSendPollVoteParams.description: Vote in (or clear the vote on) one group poll (contract revision 1.125, §4.106, capability polls; the official DataMessage.pollVote face): the anchor and selection gates run locally fail-closed; the response follows the sendPollCreate status discipline (sent/unknown, never an automatic retry).

conversationId.description: The group conversation carrying the poll (polls are group-conversation faces exclusively).

targetTimestamp.description: The poll message's sent-at timestamp; 0 answers INVALID_REQUEST.

messagesSendPollTerminateParams.description: Terminate one group poll (contract revision 1.125, §4.106, capability polls; the official DataMessage.pollTerminate face): closes the poll the anchor names; the response follows the sendPollCreate status discipline (sent/unknown, never an automatic retry).

conversationId.description: The conversation row the card rides — its kind decides the leg: a direct row routes the engine's 1:1 sendContact (recipient = the row's peer reference), a group row the groupId group leg (the calls.sendSignal addressing precedent: the connector already holds the kind, so no new parameter). A row of neither kind answers INVALID_REQUEST.

messagesSendContactParams.description: Send one contact card (contract revision 1.124, §4.105, capability send-contact; the official DataMessage.contact single-entry face): the conversation row's kind decides the leg (see conversationId). The card gates run locally fail-closed before any upstream call (the engine's parse face mirrors them, but a local refusal never spends a fan-out frame): an all-empty card answers INVALID_REQUEST (it carries nothing — empty-string name components and the empty organization are the official falsy-absent), entry arrays hold at most 64 entries, every string is bounded at 128 characters with the phone/email values non-empty, the type vocabularies are HOME|MOBILE|WORK|CUSTOM (number/email) and HOME|WORK|CUSTOM (address — the postal enum never had a MOBILE; the official client silently folds out-of-vocabulary words to HOME and the engine refuses instead, the textStyle precedent), and the avatar rides the §4.45 setProfile data-URI gate. The empty-string organization drops from the upstream frame. Unknown account answers ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried (a card whose delivery is unknown may already sit in the recipients' timelines). The response is {sentAt} — the engine's send timestamp, the calls.sendSignal ack shape; the connector keeps no send rows for the face. Structured engine errors ride the existing upstream send family; no new codes.

contactPayload.description: The official ContactAttachment shape (contract revision 1.124): name (the six official components), number/email (the value entries), address (the official postal fields), organization (an empty string is the official falsy-absent), avatar (a data:image/*;base64 URI whose bytes ride the CDN uplink as an attachment pointer — never a connector store). Every field optional; the card must carry at least one non-falsy field.

organization.description: The card's organization; an empty string is the official falsy-absent and drops from the upstream frame.

avatar.description: The card photo as a data:image/*;base64 URI within 10485760 decoded bytes (the §4.45 setProfile gate runs locally, so a malformed URI answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call). The engine uploads the bytes and the pointer lands in the card (the official EmbeddedContactWithUploadedAvatar semantics); the bytes never touch a connector store.

value.description: The phone number or email address; non-empty, at most 128 characters.

type.description: The official numberTo*Type vocabulary (both official enums share the words); optional.

contactField.description: One phone/email entry (contract revision 1.124): the value is mandatory non-empty; the type is the official numberTo*Type vocabulary (HOME | MOBILE | WORK | CUSTOM — the two official enums share numbering and vocabulary), the label a free string; both optional.

type.description: The official postal type vocabulary; the postal enum never had a MOBILE.

contactAddress.description: One postal-address entry (contract revision 1.124): the official Contact.PostalAddress nine-field shape; every field an optional string of at most 128 characters; the type vocabulary carries no MOBILE.

contactName.description: The official contact name (contract revision 1.124): the six official components, all optional strings of at most 128 characters (an empty string is the official falsy-absent).

groupsCreateParams.description: Create one new group (contract revision 1.126, §4.107, capability group-management widened in place; the official createGroupV2 posture): the engine derives the new group master key and answers {groupId, revision} — groupId is the new master key in standard base64, the id every other group face addresses. title is required non-empty ≤256 bytes (the official createGroupV2 `name: string` is mandatory the same way; the §4.104 `groupName` bound); expiration the optional timer seconds (u32; absent = the official falsy timer-off posture); avatar the tri-state update (absent = keep, null = remove, a data:image/*;base64 URI = replace — the §4.45 setProfile data-URI gate runs locally so a malformed URI answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call); members the optional initial roster (absent = create the empty group; when present the §4.44 member-array bounds hold — 1..1001 entries of 1..128 characters, an explicit empty array being the engine's own refusal mirrored locally). Unknown account answers ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried (a create whose delivery is unknown may already have created the group server-side). Structured engine errors: GROUP_CREATE_FAILED (server rejection, retryable=false, data.status? verbatim when the server gave one), GROUP_AVATAR_UPLOAD_FAILED (the group landed but the avatar upload chain failed — the {retryable, textSaved} partial-success family), STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=true). Zero local writes: the new group converges through contacts.sync like every group row.

title.description: The new group's title — required non-empty, at most 256 bytes (the official `groupName` bound).

expiration.description: Optional disappearing-message timer in seconds; 0 = off.

avatar.description: Tri-state avatar update: absent = keep (no avatar key upstream), null = remove, a data:image/*;base64 URI = replace (validated locally before any upstream call).

members.description: The optional initial roster — peer references (E.164 or service-id strings), 1..1001 entries of 1..128 characters; absent = create the empty group.

groupsMigrateParams.description: Migrate one legacy GV1 group to GV2 (contract revision 1.123, §4.104, capability group-management widened in place; the official initiateMigrationToGroupV2 posture): the engine derives the new GV2 master key from the legacy id and answers {groupId, revision} — groupId is the new master key in standard base64, the id every other group face addresses. The engine's already-migrated fallback (the put lost its race to a concurrent migration; the official hasV1GroupBeenMigrated semantic) presents as the same honest answer. groupId is the legacy GV1 group id the caller holds — standard base64 (non-empty decode; the engine pins no 16-byte length, the HKDF derivation primitive is defined over arbitrary bytes; a non-base64 or empty id answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call). title is optional non-empty ≤256 bytes (absent = the official inherit-from-local-state posture; the headless engine migrates an empty title — the engine compat §5 boundary); expiration the optional timer seconds (u32); avatar the tri-state update (absent = keep, null = remove, a data:image/*;base64 URI = replace — the §4.45 setProfile data-URI gate runs locally so a malformed URI answers INVALID_REQUEST first); members is the required non-empty V1 roster the migration carries upstream (1..1001 entries of 1..128 characters — the §44 member-array bounds). Unknown account answers ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried (a migration whose delivery is unknown may already have created the GV2 group server-side). Structured engine errors: GROUP_MIGRATION_FAILED (server rejection, retryable=false, data.status? verbatim when the server gave one), GROUP_AVATAR_UPLOAD_FAILED (the migration landed but the avatar upload chain failed — the {retryable, textSaved} partial-success family), STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=true). Zero local writes: the migrated group converges through contacts.sync like every group row.

groupId.description: The legacy GV1 group id in standard base64 as the caller holds it (the 16-byte official id is 24 base64 chars; the bound admits the padded space, the engine decodes fail-closed).

title.description: Optional migrated group title; absent = inherit posture (the headless engine migrates an empty title).

expiration.description: Optional disappearing-message timer in seconds; 0 = off.

avatar.description: Tri-state avatar update: absent = keep (no avatar key upstream), null = remove, a data:image/*;base64 URI = replace (validated locally before any upstream call).

members.description: The V1 roster the migration carries upstream — peer references (E.164 or service-id strings), 1..1001 entries of 1..128 characters.

contactsSetLocalAliasParams.description: Rename one contact as the linked account sees it (contract revision 1.10): the mutating upstream updateContact carries {account, recipient, name}, where recipient is the peer key as a single string (the pinned UpdateContactCommand reads it with getString — an array would fail upstream). peerKey must resolve to a locally known contact (a cached kind='contact' row or a direct conversation peer); anything else answers INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'updated'} when signal-cli confirmed the rename, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. No local row is modified: the alias lives in upstream account data and returns through the next contacts.sync; no event is emitted.

peerKey.description: The contact's number/uuid; must already be known to this account.

alias.description: The new display name, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes.

presenceSetTypingMessageParams.description: Send or stop the typing indicator to one conversation (contract revision 1.11). The mutating upstream sendTyping command carries {account, stop, recipient: [peerKey]} for direct conversations or {account, stop, groupId} for groups; the connector always sends the stop boolean explicitly (the null handling of an absent key is not part of the pinned upstream contract), and signal-cli expires the indicator by itself after roughly 15 seconds, so stop=true is an early clear, not a requirement. Targeting is by conversationId only; a missing conversation row answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND. The result is {status: 'sent'} when signal-cli confirmed the call, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. Nothing is written locally and no event is emitted: a typing indicator is ephemeral upstream protocol state, and inbound typing events remain a declared TODO.

stop.description: true stops an active indicator early; false (default) starts one.

historyImportStatusParams.description: Link-time history import status (contract revision 1.39, §4.38; progress extended by revision 1.54): the honest minimal projection of the backup5 archive import (ADR 0005 S3) for the desktop's S4 UI. Read-only over local state — it never touches the network. States: 'pending' (linked inside the link-time wait window, the engine's best-effort archive download has not produced the archive file yet), 'running'/'completed'/'failed' (from the persisted import row with real counters), 'unavailable' with reason 'no-archive' (wait window expired with no archive — the engine's failure modes are indistinguishable from 'the phone had nothing to transfer' and are reported as such, never guessed). Since contract revision 1.148 (§4.146) the wait-window pending resolves immediately against the engine's failure terminal snapshot: an errorCode-carrying transfer.downloadStatus face answers 'unavailable'/'no-archive' at once for the no_archive code (the phone transferred nothing — the information state, not an error) and lands an immediate persisted 'failed' row with the verbatim engine errorClass for every other code (network/cdn_unreachable/decode_failed/io/relink_requested/continue_without_upload and unseen codes, never normalized — the engine owns the word list, the connector adds no semantics); a down engine or a snapshot without errorCode keeps the pre-1.48 answers, and after history.importCancel the face answers 'unavailable' with reason 'cancelled' while the process-lifetime marker stands. While state is 'running' the result may carry progress {stage: 'downloading'|'processing', bytesTransferred?, bytesTotal?} — 'downloading' is the engine's transfer-archive byte snapshot (bytes ride together only when the engine read a content-length; otherwise stage alone, never a zero-filled guess; an errorCode-carrying failure snapshot is never a byte-progress source), 'processing' is the connector's own NDJSON import pass and never carries byte fields (the official Process stage renders copy, not numbers). Since contract revision 1.166 (§4.164) the wait-window pending may carry the same progress face — the live engine snapshot mirrored through the same shape gate, stage 'downloading' only ('processing' stays a running-row face; the engine's long-poll stretch answers stage alone); completed/failed/unavailable never carry progress, and a malformed engine snapshot or an absent/down-engine consult keeps the bare pending byte for byte. The desktop polls while state is 'running' and, since 1.166, through the wait-window pending; there is deliberately no push event in this revision. Since contract 1.56 (§4.38 attachv2) the import also persists the archive's attachment pointer faces (key material, transit CDN, integrity) into the internal attachment_locators column — never on this wire face; since contract revision 1.57 the history.attachmentDownload face walks those faces end to end (the descriptors stay metadata-only; the bytes land behind messages.attachments.open).

historyImportRetryParams.description: Manually retry one account's failed link-time history import (contract revision 1.54, §4.38, capability history-import): the official failure dialog's Retry action (Signal-Desktop installer.preload.ts retryBackupImport → backupsService.retryDownload, AGPL semantics anchor) mapped onto the connector face. Clears the account's 'failed' ledger row and re-arms the orchestration — with the archive still on the engine face the state returns to 'pending' and the sweep (next engine start) or the link watcher picks it up; attempts keep counting across retries (the ≤3 automatic budget stays supervisor-owned, the manual face is unbounded like the official dialog). Result {armed: true, state: 'pending'}. Errors: shape errors INVALID_REQUEST (retryable=false); a ledger row that is not 'failed' (pending/running/completed) answers NOT_RETRYABLE (retryable=false); no importable archive on the engine face (a failed row whose archive vanished, or no row at all with no archive — the download never landed) answers NO_ARCHIVE (retryable=false); unknown accounts answer ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND through the shared store path. Send lane, account-scoped mutating (the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier serialize it against every other account mutation) — no upstream traffic, no engine call in the retry itself.

historyImportCancelParams.description: Cancel one account's link-time history import (contract revision 1.148, §4.146, capability history-import — no new capability bit): the official cancel-sync baseline — the transfer download stops immediately — without unbinding the account. Idempotent, callable in every state. The connector registers a process-lifetime cancel marker first (the link watcher's next tick exits instead of waiting out the window; the eligibility probe refuses the account, so automatic pickup stays suppressed; no ledger row is created — a cancel never spends the ≤3-attempt budget), aborts a live NDJSON import pass through its cooperative flag (the run lands failed with the 'cancelled' error class carrying its partial counters, and only a still-running row is flipped through one conditional UPDATE so a completed run never regresses), and forwards the frozen engine contract history.importCancel {account} → {cancelled: bool} (the engine aborts its in-flight transfer-archive download). Result {accountId, cancelled, state}: cancelled mirrors the engine answer (false = nothing in flight, engine down, or engine predates the method — the forward is best-effort and never retried, the connector-side half has already taken effect); state is the post-cancel projection state ('failed' when a ledger row survived, 'running' only for a stale row, 'unavailable' when no row exists — the face never answers 'pending' again this process lifetime; importStatus renders the marker as unavailable with reason 'cancelled', and history.importRetry re-arms against the marker). Errors: shape errors INVALID_REQUEST; unknown accounts ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND through the shared store path. Send lane, account-scoped mutating (the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier, the history.importRetry class verbatim).

historyAttachmentDownloadParams.description: Download one imported history attachment's bytes from the Signal transit CDN (contract revision 1.57, §4.38 step 3, capability history-import — no new capability bit, the 1.53 precedent). The attachmentId names one descriptor of the message's received metadata (the messages.attachments.open addressing shape); the connector resolves the message locally, finds the descriptor's stored pointer face (persisted since contract 1.56 in the internal attachment_locators column), and walks the official attachv2 pipeline: cdnNumber → cdn base assembly (the official getCheckedCdnUrl map with the unknown-number fallback to CDN 0, encodeURIComponent'd cdnKey path), streamed GET (connect 10 s / total 120 s / no redirects), the ciphertext gates (trailing-MAC HMAC-SHA256 terminal check, then the whole-body SHA-256 digest face when the locator carries it), AES-256-CBC decryption (IV prefixed to the body, PKCS7), the official log-pad trim to the declared plaintext size, and the plaintextHash face over the trimmed plaintext. The plaintext lands in the governed media directory under the attachment's stable id — afterwards messages.attachments.open/readChunk deliver it exactly like any engine-downloaded file. Both integrity faces verify when both ride; a locator with only plaintextHash is the media-tier face and stays downloadable (the §4.38 ruling: its mismatch is terminal because no digest re-check remains). Fail-closed: a descriptor without a pointer face, a face missing key/cdnKey/cdnNumber/any integrity value, a malformed key or hash, or a missing/out-of-range size answers INVALID_REQUEST before any network traffic. Download, integrity, and decryption failures answer UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false — terminal, never auto-retried (§4.38 honest degradation; the official tap-to-retry face is a caller action). Local filesystem failures answer UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=true. Already-present files answer {sizeBytes} without touching the CDN (idempotent dedup: an earlier call, or the engine's own live download of the same id). Result {sizeBytes: N} — the plaintext byte count messages.attachments.open will report; no handle, no path: the bytes stay behind the chunked media triple. Send lane, account-scoped mutating ( Contract 1.98: the CDN GET rides the launcher's `KT_SIGNAL_SOCKS_PROXY` route as socks5h:// (remote DNS, the same mapping the engine child gets for `ALL_PROXY`) when the process environment carries it, the direct route otherwise; the connect 10 s / total 120 s / no-redirect posture is unchanged. (the `history-import` capability itself stays unconditional).

attachmentId.description: The attachment id from the message's received metadata (a bare attachment file name; path separators refused).

attachmentDownloadParams.description: Download one message attachment's bytes from the Signal transit CDN (contract revision 1.61, §4.54, capability attachment-download): the on-demand byte channel for message-attachment pills — the caller names the message and the descriptor's positional index, the connector resolves the row locally and walks the stored pointer face through the official attachv2 pipeline (the same machine as history.attachmentDownload, §4.38 step 3: cdnNumber → cdn base map with the CDN-0 fallback, encodeURIComponent'd cdnKey path, streamed GET with connect 10 s / total 120 s / no redirects, trailing-MAC HMAC-SHA256 then whole-body SHA-256 digest gates, AES-256-CBC decrypt with the IV-prefixed body and PKCS7, the official log-pad trim, the plaintextHash face). The pointer face resolves through the locator ladder: the live-receive column first (persisted since this revision in the internal live_attachment_locators column when the engine projects a receive locator — the engine receive face projects metadata only today, so live rows answer the hole), then the schema-18 import column (the index-aligned archive faces persisted since 1.56). Fail-closed: an index past the descriptor list, or a hole in both locator columns (a descriptor without any pointer face) answers INVALID_REQUEST before any network traffic — never a guessed download. Download, integrity, and decryption failures answer UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false — terminal, never auto-retried; local filesystem failures answer UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=true. Already-present files answer {sizeBytes} without touching the CDN (idempotent dedup: an earlier call, or the engine's own live download of the same id). Result {sizeBytes: N} — the plaintext byte count messages.attachments.open will report; no handle, no path: the bytes stay behind the chunked media triple. Send lane, account-scoped mutating (it lands a file in the governed media directory; the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier serialize it). Contract 1.98: the `attachment-download` capability is the one conditional handshake advertisement — the connector omits the tag unless its media ingest is armed, the exact gate this face answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE behind. Contract 1.98: the CDN GET rides the launcher's `KT_SIGNAL_SOCKS_PROXY` route as socks5h:// (remote DNS, the same mapping the engine child gets for `ALL_PROXY`) when the process environment carries it, the direct route otherwise; the connect 10 s / total 120 s / no-redirect posture is unchanged..

attachmentIndex.description: The zero-based position of the attachment in the message's received metadata — the descriptor list order the wire row already carries.

attachmentBackfillRequestParams.description: Request the primary device's fresh transit pointers for one message's attachments (contract revision 1.175, §4.175, capability attachment-download — no new capability bit, the 1.61 gate widened in place): the request half of the official attachment-backfill loop (Signal-Desktop AttachmentBackfill.request — the local media miss asks the primary to re-upload). The caller names the message with the same addressing attachments.download rides; the official request asks for every attachment of the message at once, so no positional index. The connector resolves the row, derives the official target triple (author = the row's sender, the account's own number for outgoing rows; the upstream sent stamp; the conversation identity as the direct peer key or the group master key), and fires the engine's requestAttachmentBackfill (SyncMessage.content oneof attachmentBackfillRequest=24 self-send). A zero upstream stamp answers INVALID_REQUEST before any engine traffic (a stamp-0 row never went upstream and cannot be backfilled). Result {status: sent|unknown} — the receipt-class posture: sent = the engine confirmed the protocol write, unknown = the engine is unreachable or refused (the write may have landed upstream; the primary's de-duplicated answer to a duplicate request is protocol-built-in, so a retry is safe). The response itself arrives asynchronously: the primary's attachmentBackfillResponse sync merges the fresh pointer faces into the row's live_attachment_locators column (empty slots only — the first face wins, the official keep-as-is posture for status/error entries), and the caller's bounded retry of attachments.download then walks the §4.54 transit chain. Send lane, account-scoped mutating.

backupsImportSnapshotParams.description: Import an official Signal Desktop local-backup snapshot for the account (contract revision 1.78, §4.68, capability history-import — no new capability bit): the counterpart of backups.export — the official desktop writes SignalBackups/signal-backup-<UTC ts>/{metadata, main, files/}, the desktop picks the directory through its own OS folder dialog, and the connector forwards the path to the engine, which verifies the snapshot metadata strictly (version 1, 12-byte IV, 16-byte encryptedId, CTR-decrypted backupId compared byte-for-byte against the account's keys) and decrypts main with the official FramesReader (HMAC tail verified end to end), producing the §4.38 history-import NDJSON the existing import pass consumes. snapshotDir is the caller-chosen absolute directory path; a relative path answers INVALID_REQUEST before any engine traffic — the connector never dereferences it, the engine is the only reader. One import task per account at a time; a duplicate start answers BACKUP_IMPORT_ALREADY_RUNNING (poll backups.importSnapshotStatus instead). The call is account-scoped mutating, so an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and never retries. Result {status: 'started'}; progress and the terminal state come from backups.importSnapshotStatus, and the watcher drives the §4.38 ledger row. Engine structured codes pass through verbatim: BACKUP_SNAPSHOT_MISSING, BACKUP_SNAPSHOT_METADATA_INVALID, BACKUP_SNAPSHOT_KEY_MISMATCH (retryable=false), BACKUP_SNAPSHOT_IO_FAILED (retryable=true), BACKUP_IMPORT_ALREADY_RUNNING (retryable=false). Wire-frame registration lands with the connector implementation batch (§4.68 plan); see backupsExportParams for the producing face.

snapshotDir.description: Absolute path of the official desktop snapshot directory (a signal-backup-<UTC ts> directory holding metadata and main); length bounded in bytes, 1..4096; relative paths are refused by the connector before any engine traffic.

backupsImportSnapshotStatusParams.description: Poll the engine's official-desktop snapshot import task (contract revision 1.78, §4.68, capability history-import): the engine's status projection verbatim minus the raw account echo — {state: idle|running|completed|failed, ndjsonPresent, startedAtMs?, finishedAtMs?, lines?, frames?, error?} with absent keys omitted rather than zero-filled; lines counts projected NDJSON rows (recipient+chat+message), frames counts archive frames including the BackupInfo meta-frame, and ndjsonPresent is the disk truth. An engine that is down or an indeterminate read degrades to the disk-truth idle projection ({state: idle, ndjsonPresent: <the archive's real disk presence>}) rather than inventing a state (the §4.46 disk-truth posture): an engine restart resets the engine-side state to idle while the produced NDJSON stays. Desktops poll while running; deliberately no push event (§4.38 precedent). Wire-frame registration lands with the connector implementation batch (§4.68 plan); see backupsImportSnapshotParams.

backupsRestoreFromCloudParams.description: Start the engine's cloud-backup restore for the account (contract revision 1.83, §4.69, capability history-import — no new capability bit): pure passthrough — the engine runs the whole chain in its own background (backup credential fetch with the 404 bootstrap self-heal → zkgroup redemption/presentation → unauthenticated chat gRPC backup location → CDN download → AEP decrypt → NDJSON at history-import-cloud.ndjson), so the connector carries only the resolved account. Result {status: 'started'} on a definite acceptance; the terminal state is observed through backups.cloudStatus (deliberately no push event). The call is account-scoped mutating, so an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and never retries. Engine structured codes pass through verbatim, the engine's CloudRestoreError::rpc_code table as the single mapping source: BACKUP_NOT_PROVISIONED / BACKUP_AUTH_FAILED / BACKUP_RUNNING (retryable=false — a never-provisioned account after the bootstrap self-heal, missing or rejected key material, the engine's own re-entry gate: poll backups.cloudStatus instead of re-starting), BACKUP_TRANSPORT_FAILED / BACKUP_DOWNLOAD_FAILED (retryable=true), BACKUP_DECRYPT_FAILED / BACKUP_EXPORT_FAILED (retryable=false). The four message-carrying families carry error.data {detail} verbatim (the engine's promised detail face); the three state families stay content-free. On a definite start — and on SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, which may actually have started — the connector follows the restore with the §4.38 consumption watcher (contract revision 1.84): the fresh history-import-cloud.ndjson is driven through the §4.38 import pass and rendered through history.importStatus (a stale archive from a previous restore is never imported; a failed phase lands the honest engine-class failed row whose retry is re-invoking this method). backups.cloudStatus stays the engine's restore-phase truth only and never claims landed rows.

backupsCloudStatusParams.description: Poll the engine's cloud-backup restore progress snapshot (contract revision 1.83, §4.69, capability history-import; read lane, the transfer.downloadStatus/backup.exportStatus read discipline): {present: false} when no snapshot exists (never started, succeeded — a success leaves no trace and its NDJSON rides the history-import chain —, or the engine restarted), otherwise {present: true, phase: 'downloading'|'failed', bytesRead, bytesTotal?, errorCode?}. bytesRead counts the CDN ciphertext bytes; bytesTotal is absent whenever the engine could not learn a content-length — honest uncertainty, never a zero-filled stand-in; the failed phase is a terminal snapshot that persists until the next start overwrites it, carrying the same structured errorCode table as the restoreFromCloud error face (the two ends share the engine's single mapping). An engine that is down or an indeterminate read answers {present: false}: the snapshot is engine-process memory, so 'not observable' is the restart truth, not an invented state. A malformed present-snapshot face fails UPSTREAM_PROTOCOL_ERROR rather than claiming absence. Desktops poll; deliberately no push event.
